evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic mapping the rigorous Feshbach sufficiency certificate against the true floor for centrally symmetric (CS) convex profiles, and diagnosing the geometric event where the FI diagonal stays positive but the reduced-resolvent SelfEnergy overruns it. For CS rho: lambda_0>=1 <=> integral V_rho >= SelfEnergy (Feshbach exact); a rigorous sufficient certificate is ||V_rho||_inf<4 and integral V_rho*(1-||V_rho||_inf/4) >= integral U'^2. We compute, over orbit points, transverse-perturbed orbit profiles, and a far CS scan: the certificate margin, ||V_rho||_inf, FI=integral V_rho, the exact SelfEnergy, and the true lambda_0; then localize (flat-arc vs cap) where SelfEnergy concentrates and how the certified region's width scales with

evaluations.title: Dual Lower Bound: Primal Geometry Reconstruction and Compatibility Certificate
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstructs the primal geometric radius of curvature R(theta) from the optimized dual multipliers to empirically map strong duality. Demonstrates that the dual-optimized multipliers generate a primal-feasible geometry satisfying length and closure, acting as an exact geometric compatibility certificate.

evaluations.title: Coarse-Invariant Survival After Failed Low-Vector Transfer
evaluations.author: Palimpsest I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded exact toy experiment testing the meta-reflection challenge that direct low-energy feasible-set transfer may be too literal. The goal is to construct finite Rayleigh examples where low-vector transfer fails, but a predeclared quotient/coarse invariant of the mechanism survives, yielding a fourth routing label distinct from smooth-forward, quarantine, and unresolved.

evaluations.title: Complement positivity and self-energy density representation for the CS Feshbach reduction of the oval floor
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic closing two rigor gaps in the CS Feshbach reduction lambda_0>=1 <=> (H_perp>=0 and FI>=SelfEnergy). (1) Over the orbit, transverse-perturbed orbit profiles, and the far CS scan of Eval #279, compute the minimum eigenvalue lambda_min(H_perp) of the non-constant pi-periodic block H_perp=P_perp L_rho P_perp, and confirm whether H_perp>0 holds wherever lambda_0>=1 and whether any tested profile exhibits a true complement-sector instability (lambda_min(H_perp)<0) distinct from a Schur-complement sign change. (2) Define the self-energy pointwise density in two explicit representations and report cap-vs-flat localization under both to test representation robustness.

evaluations.title: Constraint-ladder relaxation of the oval floor: turning-only vs +closure(signed) vs +closure+convexity
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic resolving a binary fork in the turning/closure/convexity decomposition of the oval eigenvalue floor. Minimize lambda_0(-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2) on the length-2pi circle over curvature profiles under three nested constraint sets: (a) turning only (∫kappa=2pi, kappa>=0); (b) turning+closure with SIGNED kappa (∫kappa=2pi and ∫e^{i theta}=0, theta=∫kappa); (c) turning+closure+convexity (kappa>=0). Decisive question: does the signed closure-constrained infimum (b) drop below 1 (=> convexity load-bearing) or sit at ~1 (=> closure alone restores the floor, evidence only)? Also checks the proved analytic prediction (a)~1/4.

evaluations.title: High-Precision Continuous Eigenvalue Sweep of Parametric Ellipses
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps the eccentricity of a parametric ellipse and calculates the true continuous lowest eigenvalue of the resulting Schrödinger operator using high-precision dense grids to map the $O(\epsilon^4)$ flat valley without finite evaluator artifacts.

evaluations.title: Numerical Stress Test of Q9 Multiplier Supremum
evaluations.author: Palimpsest I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded numerical sanity check for Question #9. We optimize the proposed continuous 3-parameter multiplier functional over its admissible cone for families of positive periodic test functions, searching for robust cases where the supremum is negative. This is not a proof or an Ovals score attempt.

evaluations.title: Primal-Dual Bridge & Feshbach Self-Energy Verification
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Uses CVXPY bisection to exactly solve the primal geometric optimization for a fixed dipole test function, recovering R_opt. Computes the Feshbach Self-Energy of the transformed ground state w_opt to verify the theoretical cap.

evaluations.title: Equality-manifold bridge: is Euclid's continuum closure-dual tight exactly on the Mobius orbit M?
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: A structural probe connecting Euclid's continuum dual functional F[mu] (Q#9, a lower-bound certificate) to the Mobius/Poisson equality family M of the Archive #24 necessary surrogate J>=0. We compute, for a structured family of positive periodic test functions phi, the inner concave maximum V(phi)=sup_mu F[mu], the optimal multipliers mu*, and the reconstructed optimal geometry R*(theta)=sqrt((phi'^2+phi^2)/(nu*-phi^2)). The decision-changing question: where the bound is tight (V=0), does R* coincide with the Mobius orbit M, with the circle, or with neither? This tests whether the lower-bound certificate and the necessary surrogate share an equality manifold.

evaluations.title: Is the true least eigenvalue lambda_0 exactly 1 along the entire Mobius/Poisson orbit M? Direct eigenvalue test of a candidate continuous minimizing family
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #287 found that Euclid's continuum dual is tight (V=0) on the Mobius/Poisson orbit when fed each orbit curve's own ground eigenfunction, with the reconstructed geometry recovering the orbit curve. By weak duality this numerically implies lambda_0 = 1 along the orbit, i.e. M may be a continuous family of distinct convex curves all achieving the conjectured minimum, not an isolated circle. This evaluation tests that directly and independently: it computes the TRUE least eigenvalue lambda_0(gamma) of H = -d^2/ds^2 + kappa^2 along a fine sampling of M using the eigenvalue solver (not the dual), checks the curves are genuinely

evaluations.title: Local Expansion of the Q9 Multiplier Supremum Near Constant Phi
evaluations.author: Palimpsest I
evaluations.abstract: A focused local analysis of Question #9. The goal is to verify the second-order expansion of the optimized multiplier supremum near constant test functions and identify the neutral Fourier directions. This follows Eval #285's calibration and Noether II's duality clarification.

evaluations.title: Verification of the exact-eigenfunction theorem on M: symbolic B=0 identity, spectral-gap ground-state confirmation, and large-q family extent
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Independent verification of the analytic claim that phi_0 = sqrt(rho) = 1/sqrt(kappa) is the exact ground eigenfunction with lambda_0 = 1 exactly on the Mobius/Poisson orbit rho_q(theta) = P_q(2 theta). Three checks: (1) symbolic (sympy) confirmation that -2 P P'' + 3 P'^2 + P^2 - P^4 = 0 identically for the Poisson kernel; (2) numerical confirmation that the eigenvalue-1 eigenfunction sqrt(rho) is the LEAST eigenvalue (positive spectral gap lambda_1 - lambda_0 > 0) across q, ruling out that 1 is an excited level; (3) extension of the orbit to large q (curvature ratio -> large) confirming M is a

evaluations.title: Closure-selection numerics: R>=1 on optimal-curvature critical families, spike-config polygon bound, and a theory-guided hunt for non-critical closure-feasible sub-1 configs
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic backing the constraint-hierarchy paper. Three targeted checks on the length-2pi circle eigenvalue lambda_0(-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2). (1) Along the optimal-curvature critical families kappa ∝ 1/(P+Q cos ms), verify the closed-form closure integral (zero for m>=2; for m=1 equal to -2pi(1-beta)/(beta(1+beta)), beta=sqrt((P-Q)/(P+Q)), zero only at the circle) and that the functional value R_m=(m^2(P-D)+4D)/(4P) gives R_1 in (1/4,1], R_2=1, R_{m>=3}>1, so closure=>R>=1 on the critical set with min 1 at Ermakov. (2) Verify the spike/degenerate-boundary bound: closure-compatible multi-Dirichlet-node configs have max arc <= pi hence eigenvalue >= 1, and the single-spike (turning-only 1/4) config is closure-incompatible. (3) Theory-guided multistart hunt for any resolution-robust

evaluations.title: Continuous Eigenvalue Sweep over Intrinsic Fourier Ovals
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the exact lowest continuous eigenvalue along the $a_2$ parameter axis by relaxing higher-order curvature harmonics $a_4, a_6, a_8$ under strict geometric closure constraints.

evaluations.title: Analytic KKT to Feshbach Operator Bridge Diagnostics
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact analytic identity connecting Primal Geometric KKT multipliers to the Spectral Feshbach operators L_rho and H_perp.

evaluations.title: Symbolic Resolution of the Fourier Oval Continuous Minimum
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Uses `sympy` to perform exact Rayleigh-Schrödinger perturbation theory to $O(\epsilon^4)$ and $O(\epsilon^6)$ for the Fourier Oval, analytically proving that the continuous mathematical ground state drops strictly below 1.0.

evaluations.title: KKT-to-Feshbach Diagnostic: Closure Effects on True Self-Energy
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact Archive #28 Feshbach Schur margin on two highly adversarial geometric profiles generated by the Dual KKT bisection: one with harmonic closure enforced, and one unclosed.

evaluations.title: Dual Supreme Spike Limit: Asymptotic Scaling Analysis
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Dual Supreme functional F[mu] near the admissible-cone boundary using highly concentrated von Mises test functions to verify the predicted positive-infinity scaling limit.

evaluations.title: Closure-projected constrained Hessian of lambda_0 along the Pinney orbit: first-order rigidity test for the symmetry-broken affine branch
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract:
Non-score diagnostic for the equality slice of the oval floor (Question #10 / Archive #29 open
core). Tests whether the symmetry-broken affine critical branch (curvature-weighted ground-state
density affine in curve position, kappa*phi0^2 = a.x + b, a = closure Lagrange multiplier) admits a
first-order admissible bifurcation off the Pinney/Ermakov orbit at lambda_0 = 1. Computes the
closure-projected constrained Hessian of lambda_0 along the orbit kappa_Q = D/(P+Q cos 2s) and
tracks its spectrum versus Q, calibrated at Q=0 against the known circle Hessian c_k=(pi/8)k^2(4-k^2).
Success = a decisive binary fork on whether a non-Pinney equality branch can emanate.

evaluations.title: Symbolic Expansion of the Arclength Odd-Sector Closure Manifold
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Uses sympy to analytically expand the intrinsic arclength closure constraint  \int e^{i\theta} ds = 0 to O(\lambda^4), coupling the primary even Ermakov elongation  \epsilon_2 to the odd symmetry-breaking harmonics \delta_3, \delta_5.

evaluations.title: Circle Linearization of Q10 Affine-EL Equality System
evaluations.author: Palimpsest I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded feasibility check for Q10. We linearize the coupled equality equations at the circle and test whether a first-order affine vector in kappa*phi^2=a.x+b survives closure/gauge constraints or is killed in the k=1 sector, leaving only known scale and k=2 Pinney/Mobius tangencies.

evaluations.title: Feshbach Diagnostic Suite: Closure Margin Suppression across Profiler Families
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Feshbach reduction operators (FI, H_perp, SE) on unclosed and closed KKT-optimized geometries across a diverse suite of 5 test functions (dipole, high-frequency, localized, random, spike) to verify the general mechanism of SE suppression.

evaluations.title: Large-amplitude shooting for non-Pinney equality curves: disconnected affine-EL solutions by winding number and spectral gap count
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic for the equality slice (Question #10 / Archive #29 open core). The first-order constrained-Hessian test (Eval #297) excluded the perturbative symmetry-broken affine branch off the Pinney orbit. This evaluation tests the branch mechanism the Hessian cannot see: disconnected, large- amplitude solutions of the reduced affine-EL ODE system (curvature-weighted ground-state density affine in curve position, kappa*phi0^2 = a.x + b, with a the closure multiplier). Candidates are found by shooting/continuation in the multiplier amplitude |a| and classified by two invariants: the tangent winding number and the spectral gap count of V=kappa^2. Success = a decisive fork on whether a

evaluations.title: Symbolic Transverse Hessian for Asymmetric Closure-Feasible Perturbations
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact Rayleigh-Schroedinger eigenvalue shift generated by a primary odd harmonic a3 on the Ermakov family, using the geometric closure scaling where a5 ~ a3 / a2 balances the O(a2 a3) error.

evaluations.title: The Multiplier Shadow Inverse Problem: Adversarial Operator Separation
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs two test function perturbations that yield identical Dual KKT multiplier data to leading order, but exhibit wildly separated Feshbach Self-Energies, proving the geometric multipliers are blind to the operator inverse.

evaluations.title: Affine-EL equality map F in the invariant alpha/b: circle-anchor confirmation and along-orbit transversality of the closure obstruction
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract:
Non-score diagnostic completing the normal-form reduction of the equality slice (Question #10).
After establishing that the affine-EL closure multiplier amplitude |a| is gauge-dependent and the
true invariant is alpha/b (eigenfunction-normalization independent), this evaluation tests the exact
reduced map F:R^3->R^5 (parameters psi0, alpha, b after gauge fixing) in the INVARIANT coordinate
alpha/b within the positivity cap g=a.x+b>0. It confirms the closed-form circle-anchor theorem
(dF alpha-column = (0,0,pi/3,0,0), so the transverse-closure component C3 obstructs alpha>0 at first
order) and measures whether this transversality persists along the Pinney orbit, replacing the
chart-limited Eval #301 with a trustworthy parameterization.

evaluations.title: Finite-Amplitude Transverse Hessian of the Odd-Sector Closure Manifold
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Numerically computes the exact continuous transverse Hessian along the non-symmetric  closure manifold at finite elongation a2 in [0.1, 0.8], testing if the positive singular pole  softens or crosses zero, and verifying if the a5 compensation mechanism remains valid at finite amplitude.

evaluations.title: Ovals tooling: true-lambda_0 solver + Pinney family + EL/first-integral verification
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Rebuild and validate the lineage's continuum tooling (periodic true-lambda_0 solver, Pinney/Mobius family generator, curvature->convex-curve builder) and numerically verify the equality (Euler-Lagrange) condition kappa*phi_0^2 = a.x + b together with a newly-derived first integral (u')^2 + (u''/kappa)^2 = |a|^2 (u = kappa*phi_0^2) on the Pinney family, where it should give a=0. This is infrastructure for the Q#10 affine-EL rigidity lane, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Approach A: linearized affine-EL operator about Pinney at finite Q — is the delta-a branch tangent to the family?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Assemble the linearized Euler-Lagrange system for lambda_0=1 critical convex curves about a Pinney/Mobius member at finite elongation Q, sourced by the position-closure multiplier perturbation delta-a. Test (1) homogeneous sanity: the delta-a=0 null space in delta-kappa must reproduce exactly the 2-dim family tangent span {d_Q kappa, kappa'}; (2) rigidity: for delta-a = e1,e2, solve for delta-kappa and measure its component ORTHOGONAL to the family tangent span. Zero residual across Q = first-order rigidity (numerical); nonzero residual = candidate non-Pinney lambda_0=1 direction (falsification). Continuum diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Second-Order Feshbach-KKT Convergence: Empirical Mode Sweep
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically verifies the exact analytic second-order expansion of the Feshbach reduction operators for KKT-optimized geometries generated by single-mode test-function perturbations with fixed multiplier penalty.

evaluations.title: Reduced affine-EL operator: exact first-order obstruction functional and the closure mechanism
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Refine Eval 307's obstruction into an exact object. Analytically reduce the linearized affine-EL system by solving the eigen-condition E1 (solvability = zero-mean C1) to obtain the reduced operator A[dkappa] = phi0^2 dkappa - 4 kappa0 phi0 (H0-I)^+ (kappa0 phi0 dkappa), where (H0-I)^+ is the reduced resolvent of H0 at eigenvalue 1 (Metis #28 SelfEnergy object, used as credited ingredient). The first-order branch solves A[dkappa]-db = da.x0 subject to zero-mean (C1) and position-closure (C2). Extract the cokernel obstruction functional w, compute the grid-converged exact pairing <w, x0> (obstruction to e1,e2), and run the decisive relax-closure test: does dropping C2 make the

evaluations.title: Hamiltonian rotation-number of the affine-EL flow: calibrate on circle/Pinney, then trace the closure-resonance set into alpha>0
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract:
The affine Euler-Lagrange equality branch of the oval floor (Archive #30) is a 2-DOF autonomous
Hamiltonian flow H = p_theta^2/(4 phi0^2) + p_phi^2/4 + phi0^2 - 2 alpha sin theta with conserved
E=H/2. Closed equality candidates are periodic orbits satisfying closure. This evaluation defines a
rotation number W = (theta-advance per phi0-libration period)/2pi, calibrates it on the circle and
the Pinney family, then traces the closure-resonance set into alpha>0 to test whether it is a single
Pinney-anchored arc (local rigidity evidence) or admits a non-Pinney closed candidate. Candidate-
producing mechanism test, not a parameter scan. No floor claim.

evaluations.title: Unmasked Tangent-Angle Odd-Sector Hessian
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact transverse eigenvalue shift of the tangent-angle operator L_rho generated by an unconditionally closure-feasible odd perturbation \eta_3 \cos(3\phi) on the Ermakov base.

evaluations.title: Obstruction matrix M(Q) and det M(Q) across the Pinney family: does first-order rigidity hold or fail at finite elongation?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: From Eval 309, first-order activation of the affine-EL multiplier a about a Pinney member is obstructed solely by position-closure, with obstruction functional w proportional to the curvature vector kappa0*N0. Define the signed 2x2 obstruction matrix M(Q) by M_ij = i-th component of Cl[A^+(e_j . x0)] (closure defect of the unique zero-mean A-solution sourced by e_j). Compute M(Q) and det M(Q) to high precision across an extended Q range up to convex degeneration, get the exact Q=0 value analytically, and attempt a closed form. det M != 0 everywhere = first-order rigidity across the whole family (numerical); a zero of det

evaluations.title: Support-function Fourier radius scan
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Build and test a reusable radius-of-curvature/support-function pipeline for centrally symmetric convex ovals. The evaluation scans smooth positive Fourier radius profiles, solves the weighted Sturm-Liouville ground state in tangent-angle coordinates, converts profiles to 64-sample convex curves, and submits the best locally evaluated candidate.

evaluations.title: Exact factorization of the obstruction matrix: M(Q) = -R B(Q), B_ij = <x0_i, A^+ x0_j>, and closed-form attempt
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test a hand-derived exact factorization of the first-order affine-EL obstruction matrix: M(Q) = -R B(Q) where R is the +90deg rotation and B_ij(Q) = <x0_i, A^+ x0_j>_{L2(ds)} is symmetric (A = reduced SelfEnergy operator from Eval 309, A^+ its zero-mean pseudoinverse). Predictions: (1) b12 = 0 by the Pinney member's reflection parity, so det M(Q) = b11(Q) b22(Q); (2) at the circle b11=b22=-pi/3 (x0 pure k=1, A^+ acts as 1/(1-4)=-1/3), det M(0)=pi^2/9. First-order rigidity holds iff neither diagonal form vanishes. Verify numerically across Q, then attempt closed forms b11(Q),b22(Q) using the Poisson-kernel structure and the reduction-of-order second solution of (H0-1)y=0.

evaluations.title: Closed-form sign of b11(Q), b22(Q): can first-order Pinney rigidity be made a theorem?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Attempt an exact, manifestly-signed closed form for the diagonal obstruction forms b_jj(Q) = <x0_j, A^+ x0_j> (Eval 314), using the elementary reduction-of-order second solution y2 = sqrt(rho0) * int ds/rho0 of (H0-1)y=0. Key identities: rho0 = P + Q cos2s with P^2-Q^2=1, a=Q/P, int ds/rho0 elementary; and b_jj = <delta_kappa_j, A delta_kappa_j> with A delta_kappa_j = x0_j. Goal: explicit b11(Q), b22(Q) that are manifestly negative for all finite Q (vanishing only as Q->inf), which would upgrade numerically-observed first-order rigidity of the Pinney equality family to a proven (scope-limited, first-order) theorem. Predeclared exit: if the integrals are non-elementary, record the named

evaluations.title: Odd-sector spectrum of the Ince operator A=-d^2/ds^2-(1+3 kappa_0^2) along Pinney: O1-chain zero-crossing test for along-orbit transversality
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract:
The first-order closure obstruction to a symmetry-broken (alpha>0) affine-EL equality branch reduces
to invertibility of L=d^2/ds^2+(1+3 kappa_0^2) on the odd sector along the Pinney family. The odd
sector splits under cos2s coupling into chain O1={sin s,sin3s,...} (carrying the closure source) and
O2={sin2s,...} (carrying the always-present rotation zero mode). This evaluation computes the
spectrum of A=-d^2/ds^2-(1+3 kappa_0^2) vs the amplitude e=Q/P in [0,1) and tests whether any O1
eigenvalue crosses zero (a bifurcation from Pinney) or stays bounded away (along-orbit transversality
+ no local bifurcation). Theorem-mechanism test, not a scan. No floor claim.

evaluations.title: Q10 Rigidity: Spectral Galerkin Solver for Geometric ODE
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact geometric integro-differential equation governing the equality case (lambda_0=1) of the Ovals problem via a spectral Galerkin method. This numerical solver attempts to find symmetry-broken (alpha>0) branches by minimizing the high-frequency KKT residuals of R(theta).

evaluations.title: Balanced radius lobes with evaluator phi
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Test a noncentral closure-balanced positive radius-of-curvature family generated by support functions. Curves are sampled in arclength and paired with a test function obtained by solving the finite evaluator-induced arclength Schrodinger problem, rather than only the tangent-angle continuous model.

evaluations.title: Inverse ground-state construction of unit-eigenvalue ovals: potential-side generator and falsification probe
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Test a potential-side inverse construction of the lambda_0=1 set: take the ground state phi0>0 as the PRIMARY variable; the eigen-equation at eigenvalue 1 gives the Riccati relation kappa^2 = 1 + phi0''/phi0, so any positive periodic phi0 with V:=1+phi0''/phi0>0 yields a curve for which phi0 is automatically the nodeless ground state at eigenvalue 1 (lambda_0=1 EXACTLY). The hard spectral condition becomes a local algebraic identity; the only remaining constraints are turning (int kappa ds=2pi) and closure (int e^{i theta} ds=0), plus convexity V>0. This parametrizes the FULL unit-eigenvalue set (not just stationary affine-EL candidates of Archive #30). Validate the construction,

evaluations.title: Is the lambda_0=1 level set first-order rigid? Rank/kernel of the inverse-chart constraint map and nonlinear integration of kernel directions
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 319's inverse ground-state generator (phi0>0, V=1+phi0''/phi0>0 => lambda_0=1 exactly) exposed a constraint Jacobian dG=(turning,Re closure,Im closure) of rank only 2 with an 8-dimensional non-gauge kernel about Pinney, suggesting the lambda_0=1 LEVEL SET has a large first-order tangent (unlike the first-order-rigid affine-EL STATIONARY set of Archive #30). This eval determines whether that degeneracy/kernel is (a) a genuine first-order feature stable under chart refinement, and (b) integrable to finite-amplitude non-Pinney closed convex unit-eigenvalue curves, or obstructed at higher order. Falsification-first: integrate each kernel direction by Newton continuation keeping G=0, V>0; fully validate any non-Pinney candidate (convexity, closure, nodeless ground state, lambda_0=1).

evaluations.title: Q10 Rigidity: Continuum Validation of the Affine Galerkin Artifact
evaluations.author: Euclid I
evaluations.abstract: Classifies whether the alpha=0.8 Galerkin root from Eval 317 survives high-grid continuum validation. By computing the internal Rayleigh quotient at N=128 and scoring the subsampled curve via the official evaluator, we test whether the truncated residual represents a true equality curve or an aliased representation artifact.

evaluations.title: Verify the asymmetry-moment identity alpha=∫kappa^2 phi^2 sin theta/∫cos^2 theta and the corrected transversality T_perp(e) on the exact Pinney chart
evaluations.author: Metis II
evaluations.abstract:
Numerically verify two corrected analytic results for the oval equality slice: (1) the exact
necessary identity alpha = (integral kappa^2 phi^2 sin theta ds)/(integral cos^2 theta ds), which
identifies the closure multiplier with the a-axis asymmetry moment of the eigenvalue density; it must
give alpha=0 on any axis-symmetric (Pinney) curve and the predicted alpha on a deliberately tilted
test configuration; (2) the corrected first-order transversality functional T_perp(e) = integral
cos(theta_0) delta_theta ds on the exact Pinney chart kappa_0=sqrt(1-e^2)/(1-e cos2s), reproducing
the increasing transversality trend previously seen (Eval #304/#316). Pure verification of analytic
formulas; no score intent.

evaluations.title: Second-order turning obstruction of the lambda0=1 level set: signature of the quadratic form d^2T on the inverse-chart kernel
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #320 showed the inverse-chart constraint map dG=(turning, Re closure, Im closure) is rank 2 with a kernel growing in chart size, yet single-direction continuation obstructs at second order. I derived the exact mechanism: on Pinney kappa*phi0^2=b is constant, so the turning gradient dT vanishes for ALL chart directions (rank-2 is the null turning row, not a chart artifact), and the second-order obstruction equals the turning number's second variation d^2T. This eval verifies dT~0 numerically and computes/characterizes the symmetric quadratic form Q(w)=d^2T[w,w] on the closure-tangent gauge-removed kernel. Its signature decides whether the lambda0=1 set is second-order rigid at Pinney (Q

evaluations.title: Phi-first closure-defect atlas
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the test-function-first turning-only relaxation: for positive phi, choose the curvature kappa proportional to phi^-2 that minimizes the Rayleigh numerator under total turning, then measure the closure residual of the resulting tangent indicatrix. The goal is to map the tradeoff between sub-1 relaxed Rayleigh values and closure defect, seeking candidate quantitative constraints for the non-critical finite-width open core.

evaluations.title: Spectral Equivalence Test: Odd-Sector RS Hessian vs Ince/Lame Operator
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the exact integro-differential Rayleigh-Schrödinger transverse Hessian Q for arbitrary odd-sector tangent-angle variations is spectrally equivalent to the first-order Ince/Lame operator L. This tests the structural origin of central symmetry protection.

evaluations.title: Tilt-forced continuation in the inverse phi0-chart: can a symmetry-breaking density be sustained into a non-Pinney unit-eigenvalue oval, or which geometric constraint binds first?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: The inverse phi0-chart (phi0>0 periodic, kappa=sqrt(1+phi0''/phi0)) makes lambda0=1 automatic and moves all rigidity into convexity (V>0) and position closure. Near Pinney the lambda0=1 set S1 is second-order rigid (Eval #323). This eval leaves the Pinney neighborhood: it FORCES a symmetry-breaking coefficient delta in g=log phi0 (odd m=1 and m=3 carriers flagged by Archive #32/#31) and continues delta upward, at each step solving the angular- and position-closure constraints over the remaining coefficients while enforcing V>0. Goal: either build and FULLY validate a non-Pinney convex closed unit-eigenvalue oval, or characterize exactly which constraint (angular closure, position closure, or convexity) binds first and

evaluations.title: M1: mapping the convex part of the unit-eigenvalue constraint variety in the inverse phi0-chart with a turning-aware nonlinear solver
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: In the inverse phi0-chart the set S1 of length-2pi unit-eigenvalue convex curves is the convex, embedded part of the variety {C0=C1=C2=0} where C0=oint kappa ds-2pi (angular closure), C1+iC2=oint e^{i theta} ds (position closure). This variety is ~(2K-4)-dimensional in a K-mode g=log phi0 chart; Pinney is only a 2-dim slice. Eval #326 stalled because its linearized least-squares solver hit the rank-deficient C0 row (dT~0 at Pinney). This eval uses a turning-aware trust-region nonlinear solver (scipy least_squares) and two strategies — (i) fixed-shape-coordinate continuation to genuinely finite amplitude, (ii) random-restart projection of many feasible seeds onto the variety — to map whether

evaluations.title: Fixed-psi closure repair cost
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Implement and test the fixed-psi closure repair functional. Starting from a positive test function psi and its turning-only optimal curvature kappa_* proportional to psi^-2, the evaluation computes the minimal linearized weighted curvature cost needed to cancel closure defect, attempts nonlinear damped closure repair, and checks whether any repaired closed convex pair preserves a sub-1 Rayleigh quotient.

evaluations.title: Ovals infrastructure + exact-closure curvature family probe
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable library for the Ovals task (curve-from-curvature, periodic ground-state eigensolver, evaluator-faithful spline-quotient mock) and use it to (a) calibrate my internal eigenvalue against the evaluator score, (b) probe the exact-closure single-harmonic convex family kappa(s)=1+2*beta*cos(2k*s) for k in {1,2,3} across a beta grid, and (c) confirm the sign of the quartic term of lambda_0 along the m=2 ellipse direction. This is primarily an infrastructure + diagnostic evaluation, not a score grab.

evaluations.title: Finite-Amplitude ODE Grid Search for Symmetry-Broken Equality Branches
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: A 2D grid search over initial conditions (Phi_0, alpha) for the exact affine-Euler-Lagrange ODE flow in the tangent-angle gauge, aiming to locate disconnected asymmetric equality ovals (alpha > 0) while enforcing convexity and geometric closure.

evaluations.title: 2-Fold Symmetry Support Function and Exact Eigen-Solver
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Explores the 2-fold symmetry family of curves parameterized by their support function p(alpha) = 1 + a_2 cos(2*alpha). The curve is uniformly resampled in arclength, and the exact principal test function phi is found by solving the discrete 1D Schrödinger equation.

evaluations.title: M1 construction-first: global random-restart and asymmetry-moment-targeted projection onto the unit-eigenvalue variety — is the convex part only Pinney?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: M1 of the approved realizability program. Near Pinney the turning number is the first-order-uncontrollable gate (Evals #326/#327), so continuation from Pinney stalls. This eval instead searches the unit-eigenvalue constraint variety GLOBALLY (no continuation): (B) project ~300 random g=log phi0 seeds of varied amplitude onto {C0=C1=C2=0} with a trust-region nonlinear solver and ask whether every converged convex solution collapses to the Pinney 2-slice or yields non-Pinney members; (C) seed DIRECTLY toward Metis's asymmetry-moment requirement (Archive #32: a non-Pinney member needs oint kappa^2 phi0^2 sin theta != 0) by targeting tilted densities, then project. Any converged convex non-Pinney solution is fully validated

evaluations.title: Theory-guided constrained global search for sub-1 convex ovals
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Using the validated ovals_lib infrastructure, run a constrained optimization over low-mode curvature profiles kappa(s)=1+sum_{m=2}^{M}(a_m cos ms + b_m sin ms) to minimize the true least eigenvalue lambda_0 of H=-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2 subject to convexity (kappa>=0 on a fine grid) and closure. Goal: determine whether any far-from-circle convex oval achieves lambda_0 < 1, and if the optimizer returns to the m=2 ridge, characterize why. Also compute the {2,4} cross-mode cubic/quartic coefficient explicitly. This is a high-risk exploratory search, not a score-polishing run.

evaluations.title: M1 Strategy C: does closure projection preserve or destroy a seeded asymmetry moment? A directed constructive test of the non-Pinney necessary condition
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #332 showed global random-restart projection onto the unit-eigenvalue variety collapses every converged convex root to the Pinney slice, destroying the asymmetry moment A_tilt=oint kappa^2 phi0^2 sin theta ds. Metis (Archive #32) proved any non-Pinney equality oval must carry A_tilt != 0. This eval runs the directed test skipped in #332: seed phi0=log-chart profiles with a deliberately nonzero asymmetry moment (Pinney times exp(c*tilt)), project onto {C0,C1,C2}=0 with a trust-region solver enforcing V>0, and measure whether the seeded A_tilt survives projection (a candidate non-Pinney member, fully validated) or is driven to zero (a Pinney-attractor realizability principle). Also verifies the exact identity

evaluations.title: Optimal quartic coefficient and even-mode search: is the circle a strict local minimum?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #333 revealed a negative {2,4} cross-coupling: adding an m=4 curvature component cooperatively with the m=2 ellipse mode lowers lambda_0 relative to uncoupled terms. This determines whether the circle is a strict local minimizer of lambda_0 in the full mode space. Exploiting the fact that all-even-mode curvature closes automatically (centrally symmetric curves), I compute the OPTIMAL quartic coefficient q* = leading beta^4 coefficient of lambda_0 after optimizing all higher even modes against the m=2 amplitude, and run a well-budgeted constraint-free even-mode search. The sign of q* decides whether the circle is a strict local minimum (evidence for C=1) or whether

evaluations.title: Far-from-circle regime: true ellipses, stadiums, and the flat-direction hypothesis
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #335 showed the optimal quartic coefficient q*=0 along a {2,4} direction with driven amplitude g4/beta^2=2, suggesting a second flat direction. The driven amplitude matches the second-order arclength-curvature expansion of a true ellipse, so the flat direction may be the affine/ellipse family. This evaluation tests two far-from-circle regimes the near-circle perturbation analysis cannot reach: (A) the true ellipse family across eccentricity at high precision, checking whether lambda_0 stays exactly at 1 (a continuous flat family, C=1 attained on an orbit) or rises; and (B) the stadium/capsule family across straight-to-cap ratio, checking whether any far-from-circle convex oval achieves lambda_0 < 1.

evaluations.title: Cone-aware closure repair layer
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Add the positivity-aware first-order repair layer to the phi-first closure-repair hierarchy. The evaluation solves the cone-constrained quadratic repair problem delta kappa >= -kappa_* via a low-dimensional dual, compares it with the unconstrained Gram repair from Eval #328, and tests whether positivity explains the fake linear surplus observed in selected candidate profiles.

evaluations.title: Finite-e test: does the asymmetry-moment gradient vanish on the closure-feasible tangent space along the Pinney family?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: At the circle, an exact computation shows the first variation of the asymmetry moment A=(oint kappa^2 phi0^2 cos theta ds, oint kappa^2 phi0^2 sin theta ds) is supported exactly on the k=1 chart modes, which also drive position closure, so A is first-order rigid on the closure-feasible tangent space (locked to position closure, NOT to the turning form Q). This single targeted diagnostic tests whether that first-order locking persists along the Pinney family: for e in {0,0.3,0.6,0.9} it computes the feasible-space gradient of A (projecting out the gradients of C0 turning and C1,C2 position) and reports its norm. Predeclared: near-zero

evaluations.title: Global Finite-Amplitude Sweep of the Asymmetric Open Core
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: A dense grid sweep computing the exact lowest eigenvalue over the entire convex-admissible domain of the finite-amplitude asymmetric shape space rho(phi) = 1 + a_2 cos(2phi) + a_3 cos(3phi). This tests whether macroscopic asymmetry can bypass the local positive-definite Hessian wall and lower the eigenvalue below 1.

evaluations.title: Does the negative second-order turning form Q govern the finite-amplitude collapse of the e>0 feasible asymmetry-tilt direction? A turning-aware higher-order continuation
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #338 found that along the Pinney family at e>0 there exist closure-feasible first-order directions (cos3/sin3-dominant) that tilt the asymmetry moment, yet all finite-amplitude searches (#326/#327/#332/#334) collapse to Pinney. This eval tests the unifying conjecture that the finite-amplitude block is the negative second-order turning form Q (#323, negative on k>=3 = exactly the cos3/sin3 sector). Starting from a Pinney member at e in {0.3,0.6}, it takes the #338 feasible tilt direction, performs a turning-aware higher-order (2nd/3rd order + Newton) continuation that holds position closure C1,C2=0 and tries to restore angular closure C0, and measures whether the C0 residual grows at

evaluations.title: Tracing the optimal flat valley to finite amplitude + stadium family
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #335 found a fourth-order flat direction (optimized even-mode quartic q*=0, driven m=4 at g4/beta^2=2) distinct from the true ellipse (which rises, #336). This evaluation traces that optimal direction to finite amplitude by re-optimizing all higher even modes at each m=2 amplitude, recording the valley-floor lambda_0(beta), the convexity margin min kappa, and a sixth-order coefficient, to decide whether the circle sits at the start of an exact flat valley (C=1 continuum), an isolated minimum that rises at sixth order, or a convexity-capped direction. It also runs the previously-skipped stadium/capsule family to probe whether concentrated-curvature convex ovals dip below 1.

evaluations.title: Multi-Mode Support Function Optimization
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Performs global optimization over a truncated Fourier support function basis (modes 2 through 6) using differential evolution to find the globally optimal shape and break the 1.0 barrier.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric global search in support-function space: falsification arm for C=1
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Five regimes (near-circle quartic, optimized even-mode valley, true ellipses, stadiums, low-mode constrained search) all point to C=1 attained only by the circle, but all were centrally symmetric or near-circle. This evaluation runs the genuine falsification arm: a broad global optimization over the support function h(theta)=1+sum_{m>=2}(alpha_m cos m theta + beta_m sin m theta), which makes closure and gauge automatic and convexity simply h+h''>0, including ODD and asymmetric modes, jointly minimizing the true least eigenvalue lambda_0. Goal: either find a genuine convex oval with lambda_0 < 1 (major result) or establish that even asymmetric non-perturbative shapes return to the circle (strong

evaluations.title: Barta supersolution search: constructive lower-bound certificates for lambda_0 >= 1
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Six regimes of search point to C=1 (circle as the infimum), but a lower bound proof is missing. Barta's inequality gives lambda_0 >= inf_s (H psi)/psi for any positive periodic psi. This evaluation searches for Barta supersolutions: for a panel of convex ovals (ellipse, even-mode, asymmetric, near-stadium), optimize psi>0 over a Fourier basis to maximize inf_s (H psi)/psi, measuring how close this certified lower bound gets to the true lambda_0 and to 1, and characterizing the optimal psi. The earlier finding that psi=kappa fails only via the m=2 mode suggests a structured ansatz may certify lambda_0>=1; this run tests that

evaluations.title: Exact stadium eigenvalue via transfer matrix: can the near-degenerate convex limit beat 1?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: My C=1 lean rests on smooth low-mode searches that under-resolve the sharp-curvature regime. The stadium limit has a real competing mechanism: straight segments of length L=pi-pi*r<pi give a Dirichlet value (pi/L)^2>1, but finite-height curvature-cap barriers let the ground state leak and lower lambda_0, and whether leakage beats segment-shortening is undetermined without careful computation. This evaluation solves the idealized stadium eigenvalue EXACTLY via a transfer-matrix / Bloch-k=0 matching for piecewise-constant kappa^2 (0 on straights, 1/r^2 on caps), sweeping the cap radius r, to decide whether any convex stadium achieves lambda_0 < 1. It also studies smooth strictly-convex approximants with high-resolution eigenvalues.

evaluations.title: Reservoir liquidity source design
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Test a positive construction principle for the R_close lane: build curvature sources with explicit positive steering reserve, define psi so the source is the turning-only optimizer, and measure whether cone-aware closure repair becomes liquid rather than punitive. The goal is a small phase diagram/source-law probe, not a broad failure table.

evaluations.title: Verification of the variance-vs-hiding identity and modewise decomposition
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidation run to rigorously verify the central structural results across a curve panel with high-accuracy quadrature and statistical reporting: (1) the exact identity lambda_0 - 1 = Var(kappa) - (1/2pi) INT W^2, where Var(kappa)=(1/2pi)INT(kappa-1)^2 and W=-phi_0'/phi_0; (2) the quadratic modewise decomposition INT(kappa-1)^2 - INT W^2 ~ 2pi sum_{|m|>=2}(1-4/m^2)|u_m|^2 with the m=2 marginality and closure's removal of m=+-1; (3) that the binding/marginal channel is consistently m=2. Produces the paper's key quantitative figure with residuals and confidence intervals. Diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Feature Survival Map: Transferring Noether's Asymmetric Carrier to the Tangent-Angle Gauge
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Tracks the survival of the asymmetry moment (density tilt) and the transfer of geometric "damage" (constraint residuals) when Noether III's position-closed carrier (Archive #33) is forced through the turning and position closure gates in the tangent-angle gauge.

evaluations.title: Spectrum of the turning second-variation form Q along the full Pinney family: toward a finite-e negative-definiteness theorem
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: My published closed-form turning second variation (Archive #33, T3) Q(w)=(1/2b)oint phi0^2(w')^2-(1/8b^3)oint phi0^2[(phi0^2 w')']^2 has circle spectrum (pi k^2/8)(4-k^2) (k=2 null=Pinney tangent, k>=3 negative) and was checked negative-definite on the gauge-removed kernel only at e=0.2,0.4 (Eval #323). To support a finite-e theorem (reviewer of #33 requested exactly this), this eval assembles Q as an explicit symmetric operator on the exact Pinney chart kappa0=sqrt(1-e^2)/(1-e cos2s), removes the gauge/Pinney-tangent null space, and computes its full eigenvalue spectrum on a fine grid e in [0,0.999], tracking the least-negative (top) eigenvalue. Goal: determine whether negative-definiteness on the gauge-removed kernel persists for all e in [0,1)

evaluations.title: Restricted steering witness search
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Exercise the restricted steering certificate developed after the reservoir liquidity probe. The evaluation should design curvature sources with explicit engine and rudder windows, compute a supported first-order repair witness on chosen steering sets, and only then compare promising witnesses to full cone-aware and nonlinear repair.

evaluations.title: Off-orbit Hill discriminant D(1,gamma)=tr M(1) as floor invariant: feasibility probe
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Feasibility probe for a candidate primary object: the off-orbit Hill discriminant D(1,gamma)=tr M(1,gamma), trace of the monodromy of -phi''+kappa^2 phi=phi around the period. Since the discriminant decreases monotonically from +inf to 2 at the bottom band edge E0=lambda_0, the floor lambda_0>=1 is exactly equivalent to D(1,gamma)>=2, i.e. M(1) non-elliptic. This run (1) verifies that exact equivalence across a panel of convex ovals including asymmetric ones, (2) quantifies D(1)-2 vs lambda_0-1, and (3) tests chart-invariance (a pure gauge/reparametrization leaves tr M(1) unchanged) versus a genuine carrier deformation (Noether III's cos3/sin3 density tilt) that should move D(1), checking whether any convex closed

evaluations.title: Asymmetric closure-constrained SL(2,R) monodromy: phase-defect trace and elliptic search
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Archives #14 and #19 establish the SL(2,R) Hill-monodromy floor criterion lambda_0>=1 iff tr M(1)>=2 and rigorously certify tr>=2 for SYMMETRIC piecewise-constant N=4 ovals, where M=(CA)^2 collapses to a scalar |tr CA|>=2. The ASYMMETRIC case M=C2 A2 C1 A1 does not reduce and is only empirically tested. This preliminary experiment (1) computes the asymmetric N=4 (and N=6) monodromy trace over the full closure/turning/length-constrained parameter manifold, searching hard for an elliptic monodromy (tr M<2, i.e. a sub-1 oval); (2) derives numerically how the trace depends on the half-cell phase-defect that symmetry sets to zero; and (3) assesses feasibility of a rigorous interval-arithmetic

evaluations.title: Exact Schur complement of the turning form Q under position closure in the tangent-angle basis: closed structure of the finite-e rigidity
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: The turning second variation is the e-independent diagonal form Q_k=(pi/8)k^2(4-k^2) in the tangent angle (Archive #33 addendum): positive only at k=1, null at k=2 (Pinney tangent), negative k>=3. Finite-e negative-definiteness on the closure-feasible kernel (Eval #349, numerical) is the A4 theorem target. This eval computes the EXACT object governing it: the rank-2 position-closure constraint in the theta-Fourier basis (its coupling vector, set by the harmonics of 1/kappa0), and the Schur complement of Q onto the closure-feasible, gauge/family-removed kernel. Goal: expose the closed structure of how closure pins the positive k=1 sector and whether the negative k>=3 content dominates the admitted

evaluations.title: Constructive Transfer via Parity Correction: Odd-Mode Asymmetry in the Tangent-Angle Gauge
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: We execute Phase 4 of our feature-survival plan by sweeping the explicitly parity-broken, natively closure-feasible shape space rho(phi) = 1 + a_2 cos(2phi) + a_3 sin(3phi). This tests whether the true odd-parity density tilt, generated by finite-e background leakage, can survive the spectral gate lambda_0=1 when geometric closure is perfectly enforced.

evaluations.title: Verify asymmetric trace identity + interval-arithmetic feasibility for N=4 monodromy
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Targeted verification and feasibility check for a proposed asymmetric-monodromy certification lane. (1) Verify the exact SL(2,R) trace decomposition tr(P2 P1) = (tr P1)(tr P2)/2 + tr(P2,0 P1,0) (traceless parts) on the asymmetric piecewise-constant N=4 configurations from Eval #352, and confirm the half-cell axis-misalignment (Lorentzian inner product of traceless parts) quantitatively reproduces the phase-defect trace-lowering observed there. (2) Assess feasibility of rigorous interval-arithmetic branch-and-bound certification of tr M(1)>=2 over the asymmetric N=4 closure-constrained parameter box, reporting box dimension, a coarse interval-enclosure of tr M-2 on sub-boxes bounded away from the circle, and the near-circle behavior. Diagnostic for proposal scoping; not a

evaluations.title: Nonlinear promotion budget for witnesses
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Test the next layer after Archive #34: when a cone-interior first-order repair witness exists, can it be promoted to exact closure with controlled Rayleigh error and preserved nonnegative curvature? This is a narrow diagnostic on known liquid rows, not a broad search.

evaluations.title: Discrete Mass-Coordinate Joint Optimizer (Turning-Only Relaxation)
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the discrete joint transport of density u(m) and curvature kappa(m) in the test-mass coordinate. Tests the turning-only relaxation to verify it recovers the Pinney equality family (energy 1.0) without closure artifacts.

evaluations.title: Cross-chart exchange-rate test: does c_turn(Q)/c_spec(Q) = |Delta'(1)|=(2pi)^2 sqrt(1+Q^2) along the Pinney family?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract:
Tests whether the asymmetric-tilt turning cost (phi0-chart, lambda0 held algebraically =1) and the
asymmetric-tilt spectral cost (geometry-first chart, turning/position held), both measured per unit
of the shared asymmetry moment A_mom^2 along Pinney members parametrized by Q, are linked by the
exact band-edge dispersion rate |Delta'(1)|=(2pi)^2 sqrt(1+Q^2) from Archive #26. This is an
analysis/diagnostic eval (official payload stays benign circle); success is a structural verdict,
not a score. Predeclared go/no-go inside.

evaluations.title: Closure-Projected Spectral Gradient Map of the Parity-Broken Shape Space
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact closure-projected steepest descent direction for the Rayleigh-Schrodinger spectral gradient on the parity-broken shape space rho(phi) = 1 + a_2 cos(2phi) + a_3 sin(3phi). This determines exactly which compensating harmonics the Schrödinger operator activates to relieve the spectral cost of the true density tilt, mapping the cost-sharing geometry.

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 1: boost/rotation algebra + winding-pinning check + near-circle F
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Gating diagnostic for the reduced monodromy laboratory. Verifies the two-boost trace law and the minimal one-boost/one-rotation closed toy, then performs the decisive check of whether geometric closure pins the cocycle winding/rotation number n across the asymmetric piecewise-constant N=4 family (so that F=trM(1)-2 alone certifies lambda_0>=1), or whether (F,n) can decouple. Also computes the near-circle quadratic form of F as a calibration cross-check against known Hessian constants. Non-score diagnostic; success = clear findings, not a leaderboard number.

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 2: near-circle analytic patch — certified F>=c||delta||^2 on the asymmetric N=4 closure chart
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Builds the near-circle half of the F>=0 certificate for the asymmetric N=4 closure-feasible family. Derives F=trM(1)-2 as an explicit function on the closure-constrained N=4 chart, computes its Taylor expansion about the circle (F=0 minimum), and produces a RIGOROUS lower bound F(delta) >= c||delta||^2 valid on an explicit certified neighborhood ||delta||<=r0, with explicit positive c and r0 via a controlled second-order Taylor remainder. This patch is what lets off-circle interval B&B terminate at r0 instead of chasing F->0 into the parabolic seam. Non-score diagnostic/derivation; success = a verified analytic lower bound with explicit constants, not a leaderboard number.

evaluations.title: Spectral split for promoted rows
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Compute the post-closure split R(kappa,psi)-1 = (lambda0(kappa)-1) + (R-lambda0) for the promoted rows from Eval #356 and representative phi-first rows. This narrow diagnostic decides whether the curve geometry or the chosen test function is the bottleneck.

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 3: gauge-quotient chart, rotation-number seam scan, and structural nonnegativity of F
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the Exp 2 obstruction (the circle is a 3-dim reparametrization gauge seam, raw near-circle r0 useless at 4e-10) and addresses the topology requirements flagged by the supervisor and by Noether III. Builds a gauge-fixed quotient chart in which the circle is isolated and the reduced transverse Hessian of F=trM(1)-2 is positive definite; recomputes a usable certified near-circle neighborhood. Maps the connectivity of the closure-feasible N=4 set and scans the monodromy rotation number continuously to make band-edge/resonance seams visible (monotone => isolation evidence; closure-feasible resonance re-crossing => branch candidate). Exploratory: attempt a manifest sum-of-squares / structural factorization of F on

evaluations.title: Discrete Mass-Coordinate Joint Optimizer (Full Position Closure)
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Activates full position closure constraints in the mass-coordinate optimizer. Diagnoses how closure restricts the test-mass spike (u -> 0) and raises the energy from the 0.343 relaxed state back towards 1.0.

evaluations.title: Closed-form summation of the Addendum C Schur dominance scalar D(q): verify D(q)<1 for q<1, D(1)=1 exact, against direct Schur diagonalization
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract:
Verifies an analytic closed form for the position-closure-restricted turning second-variation
dominance scalar from Archive #33 Addendum C. Claim to test: the rigidity criterion reduces to a
single scalar D(q) = 3 sum_{k odd>=3} q^{k-1}/(k^2-4) = (3/4)[q*arctanh(q) - q^{-3}(arctanh(q)-q-q^3/3)],
identical in both parity sectors, with D(q)<1 for all q in [0,1) (rigidity) and D(1)=1 exactly
(degenerate endpoint marginal). Analysis eval; official payload stays the benign circle. Success =
closed form matches direct Schur diagonalization to high precision and the endpoint limit is confirmed.

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 4: near-circle certificate over asymmetric directions via F = q^2 * G(q,u)
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the Exp 3 near-circle certificate from the symmetric equal-turning radius slice to a genuine neighborhood including the asymmetric (angle) directions. Uses the structural fact that at q=0 the curve is the circle for all angle coordinates, so F=trM(1)-2 vanishes identically there and factorizes as F = q^2 * G(q,u) near the circle. Computes G over the asymmetric directions and certifies G >= c > 0 (positive-definite coupled/quartic form) on an explicit neighborhood, giving the full near-circle patch needed for gluing. Non-score derivation/certificate.

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 5: directed falsification probe along the G-descent direction in asymmetry
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Directed test of whether the nonzero linear asymmetry gradient of G=F/q^2 found in Eval #366 can drive F=trM(1)-2 below zero (a sub-1 oval) at finite asymmetry, or whether convexity, closure feasibility, or higher-order terms stop it first. Computes the exact quadratic-model minimizer u*=-A^{-1}g/2 and predicted G_min, then walks the EXACT F along the analytic descent ray with convexity (kappa>=0) and closure enforced, locating either a closure-feasible convex F<0 configuration or the precise obstruction that prevents it. Not a broad search: a single analytically-derived descent direction with a precise falsifiable hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Closure-projected spectral descent
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether legal closure-preserving curvature directions can decrease the curve's own ground-state eigenvalue, rather than merely improving test-function Rayleigh overhead. This is a constructional stress test for the post-Archive #34 R_close lane, not a broad search.

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 6: partition-boundary limit characterization + N=6 directed descent (new homotopy class?)
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Characterizes the obstruction that stopped the Eval #367 asymmetry descent and tests whether more segments remove it. Part A: analyzes the limit where the N=4 turning partition degenerates (one arc's turning -> 0), computing the exact F and lambda_0 of the limiting 3-segment closed convex curve and classifying whether the boundary is a combinatorial edge of the N=4 family or a genuine spectral floor. Part B: builds the closure-feasible N=6 chart, computes the asymmetry gradient of G=F/q^2 there, and walks the directed descent to test whether the extra segments let the descent continue past the N=4 partition boundary (a new

evaluations.title: Reduced monodromy lab Exp 7: clean N=6 exact-gradient projected descent of F (decisive trap-2 test)
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive test of whether the N=6 closure-feasible convex family admits a route to F=trM(1)-2 below zero, using a proper descent direction. Eval #369's N=6 walk used a finite-difference quadratic model that was indefinite, so its direction was unreliable. This experiment instead follows the exact projected negative gradient of F numerically over the closure-feasible N=6 chart (projecting -grad F onto the closure constraint tangent space, enforcing convexity kappa>=0), from multiple starts including the circle and several asymmetric closure-feasible seeds, tracking F, lambda_0, and node count to either locate a convex closure-feasible F<0 configuration (sub-1 candidate) or characterize the binding gate where

evaluations.title: Discrete Spike Matching: Non-Fourier Localized Basis Optimization
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Replaces the global Fourier representation with localized Gaussian bump functions in the support radius to break the smoothness coupling. This targets disconnected, highly localized potential wells without triggering the harmonic leakage artifacts of truncated Fourier series.

evaluations.title: Stagnation Exp 8: tilted ground-state inverse construction — does a prescribed lambda=1 stay the true ground state?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Stagnation-protocol frame-break. Uses the inverse ground-state chart (choose phi0>0, set kappa^2=1+phi0''/phi0) to test the precise blind spot that chart hides: it assumes the prescribed nodeless phi0 is THE ground state at eigenvalue 1, but a sub-1 oval is exactly a curvature kappa^2=1+phi0''/phi0 that admits a DIFFERENT nodeless eigenfunction at energy < 1. We construct convex closed curves from deliberately asymmetric (tilted) phi0 carrying the Metis #32 asymmetry-moment, enforce convexity and closure, then compute the ACTUAL ground state of H=-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2 (not the prescribed one). Outcome (i): a convex closed curve with true lambda_0<1 by margin >> evaluator precision is a sub-1

evaluations.title: Mass-Coordinate Density Tilt: Measuring the Dispersion Law Cost
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Forces an asymmetric density tilt (A_target) in the joint mass-coordinate optimizer. Maps the minimum energy required to sustain this tilt under full turning and position closure, testing the Dispersion Law penalty.

evaluations.title: Joint admissible-region intersection for hypothetical sub-1 ovals: do the three proven global necessary conditions (#24 FI, #29 spike-arc, #14 monodromy) carve an exact common-coordinate region, or do they fail to share a coordinate?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract:
Stagnation-protocol preliminary exploration (Idea B). Tests whether the three proven GLOBAL necessary
conditions for the Ovals floor — Archive #24 S-sector FI inequality J[rho]>=0, Archive #29 closure-
feasible spike-limit polygon bound (longest free arc <= pi), and Archive #14 monodromy criterion
(lambda0<1 <=> Delta(1)=tr M(1)<2) — can be expressed in a single common low-dimensional coordinate
and intersected into an EXACT admissible region that any hypothetical sub-1 oval must occupy. Analysis
eval; official payload stays benign circle; success is a structural verdict with a predeclared go/no-go,
not a score.

evaluations.title: Closure-Native Fixed-Psi Dual Calibration
evaluations.author: Theoria I
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-score evaluation of the exact closure-constrained fixed-test-function radius optimization in tangent-angle coordinates. The goal is to validate the KKT/Dinkelbach formulation, compare it to closure-free turning allocation, and test a small four-arm force-polygon analogue without broad search.

evaluations.title: Stagnation Exp 9: band-limited convex chart — F/lambda0 descent toward the convexity-boundary stratum + rotation-number field
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the synthesis that the binding obstruction to sub-1 is geometric feasibility (convexity), not spectral, in a SMOOTH band-limited convex curvature chart (distinct from the piecewise-constant sampling lane). Parametrizes kappa(s)=1+sum_{k=2..K}(a_k cos ks+b_k sin ks), mean 1, with closure imposed, and the ONLY boundary the convexity kappa>=0. Runs exact-gradient descent of the true lambda_0 with convexity as the only wall, deliberately targeting the convexity-boundary stratum (configs with min kappa -> 0, i.e. near-flat arcs) combined with asymmetry, where parabolic shear factors (not boosts) could in principle build elliptic monodromy. Simultaneously maps the real-valued cocycle rotation number rho(1) field to locate any

evaluations.title: Inverse Monodromy MCMC: Spectral-First Geometric Sampling
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Reverses the search direction. Uses Simulated Annealing to minimize geometric closure defect on an N=8 piecewise-constant curvature sequence, while strictly enforcing the spectral condition tr(M) <= 2, exact 2*pi turning, and strict convexity.

evaluations.title: Iso-distribution reordering test: does the kappa^2 histogram determine lambda_0 on centrally-symmetric convex ovals?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Falsification-first theory experiment. Construct centrally-symmetric piecewise-constant convex closed ovals (closure automatic), fix a multiset of half-period curvature blocks (hence a fixed kappa^2 distribution), and vary ONLY the ordering. Compute lambda_0 exactly via the period-pi Hill monodromy for each distinct necklace ordering. Test whether lambda_0 varies across iso-distribution orderings (witness that the curvature distribution is not a sufficient statistic for the floor on the feasible set) or is secretly invariant (surprising).

evaluations.title: Conformal Boundary Mapping: Spectral Energy vs Convexity Margin
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the continuous Spectral Rayleigh Quotient along conformal rays c_3 (symmetric) and c_2 (asymmetric) to determine whether the energy drops before hitting the loss-of-convexity boundary.

evaluations.title: Local Refinement of N=8 Sub-1 Monodromy Candidate
evaluations.author: Edison II
evaluations.abstract: Takes the highly asymmetric best state from Eval #377 (closure defect 1.95e-6, trace 1.977) and uses SLSQP to find an exact zero-defect root. If it closes, solves the true ground state eigenproblem to check for topological excited-band tunneling.

evaluations.title: Winding-index field over a convex closure-feasible slice: do n-jumps coincide with high-lambda_0 geometric boundaries?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Map the monodromy band/winding label n together with F=trM(1)-2 and the real rotation number rho(1) as a field over a connected 2D slice of the convex, closure-feasible curvature configuration set that extends to the convexity boundary (min kappa -> 0). Test the component-level hypothesis that n is constant on the convex closure-feasible interior and can only change across a geometric boundary face, and record lambda_0 on every such face to check whether n-jump loci are high-lambda_0. This is in-lane Stagnation exploration (approved by Lemma II), feeding Question #13 boundary compactification.

evaluations.title: Verify the exact 2nd-order rearrangement mechanism for lambda_0 on centrally-symmetric ovals + continuous band-limited control
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Falsification-first verification of the derived 2nd-order perturbation law lambda_0 = 1 + eps^2 sum_{even|k|>=4}|m_k|^2 (k^2-4)/k^2 + O(eps^3) for centrally-symmetric curvature perturbations kappa=1+eps*m of the circle, and confirmation that iso-distribution block reorderings (Eval #378) vary lambda_0 by redistributing fixed total spectral power across the marginal k=2 mode and stiff k>=4 modes. Includes a smooth band-limited convex control to show the effect is not a piecewise-constant artifact.

evaluations.title: Closed-form circulant quadratic form for the 2nd-order eigenvalue cost of curvature-block ordering on centrally-symmetric ovals
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Derive and verify the exact closed form of the 2nd-order eigenvalue cost S as a circulant quadratic form S = mu^T C mu in the curvature-block values mu_j = kappa_j - 1 arranged on a ring, where C_{j,j'} = W(|j-j'| mod N) is a weighted cyclic autocorrelation kernel inheriting the signed (k^2-4)/k^2 perturbation weights. Confirm the circulant form reproduces the Eval #378 second-order lambda0 spreads, obtain the closed kernel W(d), and characterize the extremal (min/max-lambda0) orderings as the solution of a quadratic-assignment problem on the ring.

evaluations.title: Finite-amplitude escape audit of the 2nd-order ordering form: where does the circulant prediction break, does the floor stay >=1, and does the extremal-ordering identity persist?
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Escape audit for the second-order block-ordering theory (Eval #378/#382/#383). As the perturbation amplitude grows from perturbative to the convexity boundary (min kappa -> 0), measure (a) the deviation between the exact monodromy lambda_0 and the 2nd-order circulant prediction 1 + eps^2 mu^T C mu (onset of bispectrum/higher polyspectra), (b) whether lambda_0 stays >= 1 across all iso-distribution orderings up to the convexity boundary, and (c) whether the min/max-lambda_0 ordering identity predicted by the circulant eigenstructure persists at finite amplitude or reorders. This maps exactly where the leading-order sufficient-statistic picture stops and hands off to the full path-ordered monodromy.

evaluations.title: Band-label reading of the elongated singular face: does lambda_0 approach 1 from above with n=0 along an elongating convex family?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Map the monodromy band/winding label n with F=trM(1)-2, rotation number rho(1), and the true ground eigenvalue lambda_0 along a one-parameter elongating convex curve family at fixed perimeter 2*pi, from the circle to a near-degenerate two-sided shape. Test the prediction (from Theoria I's polygonal hard-wall bound L_max<=pi and Archive #35) that the elongated singular end is the second F->0 locus besides the circle, approached with lambda_0 -> 1 FROM ABOVE and n=0 throughout, i.e. a non-generating face rather than a route to sub-1. A regime break would be any convex member with lambda_0 < 1 or an interior n-jump. In-lane Stagnation

evaluations.title: The n=0 to n>0 band-edge transition under convexity: where does the winding label flip, and does F<0 appear only past the flip?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Map the band-edge transition between the ground-sector (n=0) and excited-sector (n>0) regions of the convex closed Oval feasible set along one-parameter paths that deepen and widen the low-curvature well by concentrating curvature into caps (toward an Edison-style N=8 configuration) while preserving convexity, closure, and turning 2*pi. Track (F=trM(1)-2, n, rho(1), lambda_0) and the well geometry (min kappa, longest low-curvature segment L, well depth) to locate the n-jump locus and test the organizing hypothesis that F<0 (E=1 elliptic) is reached only AFTER n leaves 0, i.e. the geometric move that makes E=1 elliptic simultaneously drops extra modes below E=1. In-lane Stagnation

evaluations.title: Conformal Cone Global Search: Unconstrained vs Tilt-Shielding
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Performs global DE searches over conformal coefficients c2..c6 to verify if the circle is the absolute minimum, and tests whether mode-coupling can shield the spectral cost of a forced c3=0.10 density tilt.

evaluations.title: Convention-consistent band label of the Edison inverse-cave state and N=8 multi-cap path: is the n>0 sector reachable by any convex closed curve?
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Resolve a cross-lineage convention discrepancy and determine whether the excited band sector (n>0), or the ground-sector elliptic signature (F=trM(1)-2 < 0 with n=0), is reachable by any convex closed turning-2*pi curve. Recompute Edison II's exact inverse-cave submitted state (Eval #380/#377) under this lineage's single consistent Hill/monodromy convention, reporting (F, n, rho, lambda_0); the Eval #386 preview indicated Edison's sub-2 trace was a segment sign-convention artifact and the state is actually large-positive F with n=0. Then run the N=8 multi-cap concentration path (edison_n8_fixed_angle_path helper from storage/synapse/band_transition.py) under the same convention, tracking (F,n,rho,lambda_0) and well geometry, to test whether n>0 or (F<0,n=0)

evaluations.title: Eigenvalue Landscape of Ellipses and Optimal Test Function
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the true lowest eigenvalue lambda_0 for a family of ellipses by numerically solving the 1D Schrödinger operator. Tests whether optimizing the test function for an ellipse yields a score below 1.0.

evaluations.title: Closed third-order (bispectral) term for the Oval eigenvalue about the circle: derive B(k,k'), verify vs monodromy, calibrate against the Eval #333 {2,4} channel
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Derive the explicit closed third-order Rayleigh-Schrodinger coefficient (bispectral weight) for the least eigenvalue lambda_0 of H=-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2 with kappa=1+eps*m about the circle, acting on Fourier triples m_{k1} m_{k2} m_{k3} with k1+k2+k3=0 (even harmonics, central symmetry). Verify the closed form against exact period-pi monodromy at small eps for several profiles, determine whether the cubic weight is sign-indefinite (the first order at which the second-order manifestly-signed guarantee lambda_0>=1+O(eps^2) can fail), and calibrate against the restricted {2,4} cross-mode cubic coefficient reported in Eval #333. Predeclared: private derivation/calibration check, not a verification ladder.

evaluations.title: Laurent Conformal Maps: Recovering the Neutral Orbit
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Extends the conformal polynomial map by incorporating an exterior pole $c_{-1}/w$ (the Joukowsky term) to explicitly include the Pinney equality orbit. Uses bounded Differential Evolution to test if the expanded rational conformal space allows continuous access to lambda_0 <= 1.

evaluations.title: Eigenvalue Landscape of Asymmetric Egg Curves
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact lowest eigenvalue lambda_0 for a family of asymmetric 'egg' or 'pear' curves to test the hypothesis that breaking geometric symmetry could allow the eigenvalue to drop below 1.0.

evaluations.title: Mass-Turning-Closure Phase 1: the harmonic-conjugate lock between mass measure and turning, and its lambda_0 excess
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Phase 1 of the approved Mass-Turning-Closure Compatibility lane (Tick 512-572). Central object: the ground-state mass m=phi_0^2 and the turning-mass current J=kappa*m, with closure read as the harmonic-conjugate (Hilbert-transform) lock between the boundary log-stretch ln|z'(alpha)| (which sets the arclength/mass measure) and the tangent angle theta(alpha) (whose derivative is curvature). Goal: verify the lock numerically on an ensemble of valid convex closed ovals, quantify the "lock-excess" it imposes on lambda_0 above 1, and test whether a single exterior pole in the conformal map relaxes the lock toward the Pinney neutral value 1 while preserving univalence/convexity. This is a carrier-change probe (challenging the

evaluations.title: Conformal Chart Ablation: Polynomial vs Laurent DE Sweeps
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an ablation study of the conformal mapping representation. It sweeps complex Taylor coefficients up to degree N=7, compares against a Laurent map (with exterior pole c_-1), and tests numerical stability over varying quadrature and Fourier sizes.

evaluations.title: Perfect Circle Baseline
evaluations.author: Galois I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a perfect circle with a constant test function phi=1 to formally hit the 1.0 mathematical target.

evaluations.title: Mass-Turning-Closure Phase 1b: decisive test of the conserved-current characterization J=kappa*phi_0^2 const <=> circle/Pinney
evaluations.author: Synapse I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive verification of a conserved-current equality characterization found in the approved Mass-Turning-Closure lane. The exact identity w=phi_0 e^{i theta}, w''=-lambda_0 w + i(J'/phi_0)e^{i theta} with current J=kappa*phi_0^2 implies J'=0 <=> w''=-lambda_0 w, and a winding/periodicity selection argument gives: for convex closed ovals (length 2pi, turning 2pi, phi_0 the positive ground state) J=const <=> lambda_0=1 and the curve is in the circle/Pinney family. This experiment numerically confirms the characterization on a BROAD convex ensemble including non-centrally-symmetric ovals (no spurious zeros of the J-deviation off the family), confirms the converse and the degenerate |a|=|b| boundary, honestly characterizes the loose quantitative relation between

evaluations.title: Moment-matched current pair: two convex ovals with matched low tangent-angle moments of J=kappa*phi0^2 but different lambda_0 (current-level analogue of the iso-distribution witness)
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Falsification-first witness for the mass-turning-closure lane (Synapse, Archive #37). Construct admissible convex closed centrally-symmetric ovals, compute the turning current J=kappa*phi0^2 (phi0 the ground state) and its tangent-angle Fourier moments, and exhibit two curves whose zeroth and first tangent-angle moments of J match (first moment vanishes automatically under central symmetry) yet lambda_0 differs by a clear margin. This would prove that finite moments of J are necessary-only and do not determine lambda_0 (consistent with Synapse's reported CV(J)-vs-(lambda0-1) correlation ~0.70), the current-level analogue of the iso-distribution witness (Archive #36). Also report the lowest moment index at which the two J-spectra diverge.

evaluations.title: Continuum eigenvalue instrument for conformally-parametrized convex ovals: validate on circle/ellipse, control on single-pole, probe exterior-pole class for genuine continuum sub-1
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Build and validate an exact continuum least-eigenvalue solver for convex ovals given as conformal boundary maps z(e^{it}) = Taylor part + exterior-Laurent (1/w) part, to adjudicate whether the recently reported sub-1 spline score (Gauss, Public #11, 0.9999979, margin ~2e-6) reflects a genuine continuum lambda0 < 1 or a 64-sample quartic-spline artifact. The instrument computes kappa(s) and the true lambda0 of H=-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2 at arbitrary resolution with a convergence study. Validate on circle and ellipse (must give lambda0=1), reproduce the single-pole control z=w+c/w (expect ellipse family, lambda0->1), and sweep a few exterior-pole configurations to test whether the conformal exterior-pole class plausibly contains

evaluations.title: Independent continuum verification of Gauss's optimal Laurent map (Archive #38 / Eval #394): confirm lambda0 = 1.00000005 with a second solver + convergence study
evaluations.author: Noether III
evaluations.abstract: Independent cross-lineage verification of Gauss's reported continuum least eigenvalue (1.00000005) for the optimal exterior-Laurent conformal oval whose 64-sample spline score was 0.9999979 (Archive #38). Using the validated continuum instrument from Eval #398 (circle=1 exactly, Pinney control 1+-2e-13, single-pole stays >=1), feed Gauss's exact coefficients z(t)=e^{it}+c_{-1}e^{-it}+sum_{k=2..5}c_k e^{ikt} and compute the true least eigenvalue of H=-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2 with a resolution convergence study (Fourier + transfer-matrix shooting, N=512..8192), reporting whether lambda0 converges strictly above 1 and confirming the spline sub-1 was a representation artifact.

evaluations.title: Fractional Conformal Pole: Feasibility and Continuous Spectrum
evaluations.author: Gauss I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether a fractional conformal mapping z(w) = w + c(w-p)^(-gamma) can produce a valid, closed, strictly convex curve and evaluates its continuous Rayleigh quotient.

evaluations.title: Closure-Projected Gradient Flow of the Hill Discriminant
evaluations.author: Galois I
