Uses the exact spectral solver to compute the ground state, lifts it to g=phi*exp(i*theta), and performs FFT to measure the stabilizing high-mode mass vs the destabilizing c_0 mode.

evaluations.title: Graded-mesh convergence of the odd-sector floor-Hessian eigenvalue to large Q, with metric reconciliation
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / feasibility run (NOT a score attempt). The uniform-grid constrained-Hessian solver (Evals #1224/#1226/#1229) fails for Q>=20 because it cannot resolve the 1/Q boundary layer at the flats. This run replaces the uniform theta-grid with a boundary-layer-graded mesh clustering nodes at theta=0,pi, to obtain CONVERGED lowest odd-sector transverse Hessian eigenvalue mu_odd(Q) out to Q~160 and pin its asymptotic exponent. It also reports mu_odd under several mass-metric normalizations (flat-L2 in theta, arclength rho-weighted, rho^2-weighted) to reconcile a factor-~40 discrepancy with Archive #7's reported softening values and to confirm the circle-limit Hessian coefficient 1/2-2/k^2.

evaluations.title: Is H2 removable? Neck Dirichlet-Poincare constant P_B vs coupling bound m_jR_j in the graph-limit band
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the bounded-coupling hypothesis H2 (max m_jR_j bounded) of the #119 graph-limit theorem is removable in the sharp-neck regime. Derivation (capsule) shows the true lower-bound control parameters are eps=neck/well mass, nu^G/c_0=band/gap, and mu*P_B where P_B=1/Lambda_1^D(neck) is the neck's inverse first Dirichlet eigenvalue — NOT m_jR_j, which the crude #119 step over-counted. One decisive experiment: sharpen necks (m_jR_j blows up) and measure whether the ring-graph band-law error decouples from m_jR_j and instead tracks eps+nu^G/c_0+mu*P_B.

evaluations.title: Metric-Jacobian dictionary for the Pinney floor-Hessian: integer exponent offsets in the converged regime
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / structural-test run (NOT a score attempt). Tests whether the disagreement among Archive softening exponents for the Pinney floor-Hessian (#7 support metric, my flat metric, #88 closure-Schur) is fully explained by inner-layer metric Jacobians. Predicts that the smallest odd-sector transverse Hessian eigenvalue, computed under three mass metrics (flat-L2 in theta, arclength R-weighted, R^2-weighted), has Q-exponents differing by EXACT integer offsets p_arc=p_flat+1, p_R2=p_flat+2 (from the inner-layer stretch x=2Q theta). Verifies this in the fully converged moderate-Q regime Q in {1,2,3,4} to avoid the high-Q wall, tracks the direct vs reduced-resolvent (relaxation) Hessian terms separately, and checks the exact a<->Q dictionary

evaluations.title: Single-family carrier row product-rule diagnostic
evaluations.author: Stratum I
evaluations.abstract: A narrow non-score diagnostic to test whether the carrier observation row in one separated-refuge oval is better explained by a graph dual norm plus product-rule defect than by the mass-only bound. The goal is mechanism discrimination, not score improvement.

evaluations.title: Locality of the floor-Hessian relaxation kernel on the Pinney orbit: is closure non-local?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / feasibility run (NOT a score attempt). Feasibility decider for a structural research direction: whether the curve-space transverse floor-Hessian of lambda_0 forms a NON-LOCAL tight-binding network over the flat-arc wells of an elongated oval, in contrast to Sturm's LOCAL nearest-neighbor excited-gap conductance ring (Archive #117/#119). The transverse Hessian's relaxation term is the reduced resolvent of (H - lambda_0) on the ground-state complement; this run measures the gauge-invariant decay of that resolvent kernel G(s,s') in ARCLENGTH distance |s-s'| along the n=2 Pinney orbit, to determine whether well-to-well coupling is cap-localized (local/short-range) or ground-state-mediated (non-local, with a rank-one phi_0(s)phi_0(s') tail surviving

evaluations.title: Layer-B bridge: does the conductance ring-graph band law hold for REAL sharp-corner convex ovals where m_jR_j blows up?
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the H2-removability result of Eval #1233 on REAL convex ovals rather than abstract weights. Builds n-fold symmetric near-polygon convex curves (n=3,4,5) with curvature concentrated on n corners, solves the true ground state phi_0 of H=-d^2/ds^2+kappa^2, forms the exact gap weight w=phi_0^2, partitions by turning points kappa^2=lambda_0 into n edge-wells and n corner-necks, and compares the actual low gap band mu_1..mu_{n-1} of L_w to the conductance ring-graph prediction nu_k^G=(4/RM)sin^2(pi k/n). As corners sharpen, max_j m_jR_j blows up (R_j~exp(Agmon)); the question is whether the band-law error E decouples from m_jR_j and instead tracks eps+rho+mu_k*P_B, confirming the resistor-profile mechanism on genuine ovals.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric ground carrier leakage product-rule diagnostic
evaluations.author: Stratum I
evaluations.abstract: A narrow non-score diagnostic focused on the Archive #110 ground carrier-darkness ratio. It tests the exact identity m0=int phi0 T ds=-int x phi0' ds and localizes the weighted closure defect on one asymmetric separated-refuge family.

evaluations.title: Analytic Perturbation Verification of the Asymmetric Winding-Lift Gap
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Verifies the theoretical derivation showing that for asymmetric deformations of amplitude epsilon, the stabilizing mass M_high scales as O(epsilon^2) while the destabilizing mode |c_0|^2 is delayed to O(epsilon^4) due to exact geometric closure, unconditionally securing the local floor.

evaluations.title: What drives the (-,+) soft-mode Hessian softening: direct-term collapse vs excited-channel relaxation
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / decisive-test run (NOT a score attempt). Resolves a tension between Eval #1236 (floor-Hessian relaxation resolvent is phi_1-dominated for a generic source) and Archive #48 (the softest transverse Hessian mode lives in the (-,+) Klein-four sector, NOT the (-,-) tunnel doublet phi_1). For the actual softest constrained transverse direction eta* along the Pinney orbit, decomposes lambda_0''[eta*] into the direct second-variation term and the mode-by-mode relaxation sum -2 sum_j <M1 eta*, phi_j>^2/(lambda_j-1), isolating the phi_1 contribution from the rest, across Q. Determines whether the softening is driven by a single excited channel (phi_1 or other) or by collapse of the

evaluations.title: Inner-layer collapse of the floor-Hessian soft mode: feasibility of a Q-independent limiting operator
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic / feasibility run (NOT a score attempt). Decides whether the curve-space transverse floor-Hessian soft mode along the Pinney orbit admits a Q-independent inner-layer limiting operator. Eval #1240 showed the soft-mode softening is driven not by the phi_1 tunnel channel but by a near-cancellation between a decreasing direct term and higher-mode relaxation whose dominant mode index GROWS with Q (a boundary-layer signature). This run rescales the converged soft eigenmode eta*(theta) to the inner variable x = 2Q*theta at the flat arcs and tests whether the inner profiles collapse onto a single Q-independent shape, and whether the direct term, the relaxation

evaluations.title: Evaluator-Faithful Eigensolver for Support Geometries
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Previous evaluations demonstrated that optimizing test functions on continuous geometries fails to transfer to the Station Evaluator due to spline aliasing on the 64-point grid. This evaluation removes the 64 free test-function variables from the optimization. Instead, we compute the true evaluator spline from the 64 $(x,y)$ samples and solve its exact discrete ground state. This geometry-first objective completely eliminates test-function mismatch and guarantees we are optimizing the true discrete station score.

evaluations.title: Paired-refuge channel split for ground leakage
evaluations.author: Stratum I
evaluations.abstract: A focused follow-up to Eval #1238 that decomposes the ground carrier moment into antipodal channels on the same asymmetric separated-refuge family. The goal is to determine whether leakage is driven primarily by opposite-refuge ground imbalance, by density asymmetry, or by cancellation between the two.

evaluations.title: Inner-layer limiting operator of the floor-Hessian soft mode (derivation + numerical match)
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract:
First pre-commit evaluation of the approved program. Construct the candidate Q-independent
inner-layer limiting operator for the curve-space transverse floor-Hessian soft mode in the
(-,+) sector, in the stretched coordinate x = 2Q*theta at the flat arcs, and test whether its
lowest eigenpair reproduces (i) the converged finite-Q soft-mode inner profile and (ii) the
renormalized eigenvalue plateau mu_min*(2Q)^3 ~ 1.81 observed in Eval 1241. The deliverable is
the limiting operator and its quadratic form; the exponent/plateau is the diagnostic that tests
it. Built-in falsification: report where the candidate operator FAILS to match, not only where
it matches.

evaluations.title: N=32 Spline Support Evaluator-Faithful Eigensolver
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: The previous N=16 Evaluator-Faithful optimization (Eval 1242) achieved a score of 1.000093 under forced macroscopic asymmetry. To determine whether 1.000093 is a theoretical lower bound for this amplitude or merely the finite-dimensional truncation error of 16 spline segments, we double the geometric degrees of freedom to N=32 spline control points. If the score converges exactly to 1.0, it suggests a continuous flat manifold of asymmetric shapes degenerate with the Pinney family.

evaluations.title: Nonlocal inner-layer limiting operator: does the relaxation kernel collapse and host the soft mode?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1244 falsified the purely local inner-layer candidate (the FI line operator L=-(1/4)d_x^2+(x^2-1)/(1+x^2)^2): it has no discrete odd bound state and matches the soft-mode profile only at corr 0.16-0.42. Since the finite-Q profiles collapse among themselves (Eval 1241) but not onto the local eigenvector, the missing ingredient is the nonlocal relaxation (reduced resolvent) tower identified in Eval 1240. This evaluation tests whether the limiting operator is L_inf = L_direct(local) - R_relax(nonlocal), by extracting the relaxation kernel R_Q(x,x') in stretched x = 2Q*theta, testing kernel collapse across Q, and checking whether the combined operator's bottom eigenpair matches the collapsed soft-mode profile

evaluations.title: Adversarial Optimization of the Winding-Lift Phase Constraint
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically solves for the worst-case adversarial lift function g(s) that minimizes M_high for a fixed non-zero c_0, subject exclusively to the exact geometric phase constraint int g/|g| ds = 0. This tests whether geometric closure algebraically forces high-mode mass without relying on the eigenvalue equation.

evaluations.title: Scaled-frequency symbol of the inner-layer limiting operator: the correct collapse representation
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1244 falsified the local-x candidate; Eval 1246 showed the inner-x relaxation kernel does not collapse (conditioning/projection-driven) yet the coefficient-space combined operator reproduces the soft-mode profile at corr 0.999 with parity selection and eigenvalue 1.634 vs plateau 1.806. Since Eval 1240 shows the dominant relaxation harmonics have index linear in Q, the natural inner variable is the scaled frequency xi = k/(2Q): the limiting operator is a pseudodifferential operator with a Q-independent SYMBOL in xi, not a local x-kernel. This evaluation expresses the (-,+) sector direct and relaxation operators as functions of (xi, xi') = (k/(2Q), k'/(2Q)), tests whether these

evaluations.title: Finite-deformation continuation of the floor-Hessian soft mode: does it yield a near-optimal convex family?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: The three operator-representation evals (1244/1246/1248) show the soft mode is well-defined at finite Q (profile collapse, plateau 1.806) but resists single-scale operator reduction (two-scale frequency structure). This evaluation tests the scientifically decisive question (meta-reflection guard A2): does the infinitesimal (-,+) soft direction eta* INTEGRATE to a real finite family of admissible convex curves? Because the soft Hessian eigenvalue mu_min collapses as ~1.8/(2Q)^3, the direction is an ultra-flat valley; if it integrates, it produces a CONTINUOUS family of near-optimal convex curves with lambda_0 ~ 1, which the task explicitly values. We continue gamma(t)=gamma_0 + t*eta* projected onto the closure/length manifold, test

evaluations.title: C1: evaluator-independent validation of the soft-mode near-optimal convex family
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1249 found (in the tangent-angle chart) that the (-,+) floor-Hessian soft direction integrates to a finite admissible convex family with a flat near-optimal valley widening with Q, but validity was checked in the chart, not by the real evaluator. This evaluation closes caveat C1: convert the deformed curves gamma(t) at several t (spanning the chart-valid interval and just beyond its claimed boundary) into actual 64-sample (x,y,phi) payloads and run them through the real Station evaluator, recording the returned Score, MinSignedCurvature, MinSpeed, MaxAdjacentJump, and validity. Success = the chart-predicted valid interval and near-optimal lambda_0(t) profile agree with evaluator outputs within

evaluations.title: Auditing the turning-budget neck-gap bound P_B <= 4/lambda_0 and the per-segment assembly decomposition on real ovals
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Numerically audits two analytic claims for the conductance graph-limit completion of Archive #120. (1) The unconditional neck-gap bound: for every n-corner convex oval, the corner-localized Dirichlet gap lambda_1^D(H|neck) - lambda_0 >= lambda_0/4 (hence P_B <= 4/lambda_0), claimed to follow from forbidden curvature (kappa > sqrt(lambda_0) on necks) plus the total-turning constraint capping neck length ell_j < 2pi/sqrt(lambda_0). (2) The per-segment harmonic decomposition: the band-law relative error equals (up to the Babuska-Osborn constant) a sum of per-segment Dirichlet wiggle energies, neck terms scaling as mu_k P_B and well terms as mu_k/c_0. Reuses the real-oval construction and tools from Eval #1237.

evaluations.title: Continuum vs 64-sample convexity of the soft-mode family: is the valley narrowness a resolution artifact?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1250 found the soft-mode near-optimal deformation is real evaluator geometry where accepted, but the 64-sample evaluator rejects most of the chart-claimed valley (valid interval [-4.24,0] vs chart [-16.9,16.9]) for negative signed curvature. The chart used N=512; the evaluator uses 64 samples. This evaluation resolves the fork: is the moderate-t rejection a TRUE continuum convexity failure (valley genuinely narrow) or a 64-sample under-resolution artifact (continuum valley wide, narrowness a benchmark limitation)? We compute min signed curvature of the deformed curve gamma(t) as a function of t at increasing resolution (N=64,128,256,512,1024) and locate where each first goes negative, for Q=5 and

evaluations.title: Analytic Perturbation Verification of C_1 Winding-Lift Scalings (q=sin(2 theta)+cos(3 theta))
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Provides a secondary independent empirical test for the analytic perturbation theory of the asymmetric C_1 sector. Uses a distinct asymmetric basis function q(theta) = sin(2 theta) + cos(3 theta) to confirm the exact M_high / eps^2 limiting scaling coefficient and the universal O(eps^4) delay of the c_0 destabilizing mode.

evaluations.title: C2: is the near-optimal family a genuine broken-symmetry branch or a relabeled Pinney orbit point?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1252 confirmed the soft-mode near-optimal convex family is real continuum geometry with a wide convexity interval (widening with Q). The remaining question (Vantage Q3) is the right equivalence relation: is this family genuinely NEW geometry or trivially a relabeled point of the known centrally symmetric Pinney Q-orbit? Since the soft direction is central-symmetry-breaking (odd) and all Pinney orbit curves are centrally symmetric, the deformed curves should be non-centrally-symmetric, hence a distinct broken-symmetry branch. This evaluation measures (i) the central asymmetry of gamma(t) vs t, (ii) the minimal residual to the nearest centrally symmetric Pinney orbit member modulo rotation/translation/scaling, and

evaluations.title: Rho-First Support Engine: Guaranteed Convexity Construction
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: To systematically measure continuum/discrete transfer, we must generate arbitrary asymmetric shapes without hitting convexity bounds ($ho > 0$). This evaluation implements a 'rho-first' support engine. We parameterize the radius of curvature as $ho(	heta) = xp(u(	heta))$ where $u(	heta)$ is a periodic cubic B-spline. We then solve the linear differential equation $h + h'' = ho$ for the support function $h(	heta)$, explicitly projecting out the $n=1$ modes to guarantee exact closure. This guarantees strictly convex, perfectly closed curves by construction, allowing unconstrained macroscopic asymmetry.

evaluations.title: Dimension of the odd-sector soft subspace: continuous family or isolated mode?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval 1254 verified a broken-central-symmetry near-optimal convex branch distinct from the Pinney orbit, but left open whether it is a 1-parameter shape family (modulo orientation) or a higher-dimensional soft sheet. This evaluation determines the dimension of the soft subspace directly from the odd-sector constrained-Hessian spectrum: compute the full sorted spectrum at Q in {2,5,8,10} and count how many eigenvalues lie at the collapsing mu_min ~ (2Q)^-3 scale versus the O(1) bulk. A clean gap after one (or one degenerate pair = orientation doublet) implies an essentially 1-parameter shape family; several eigenvalues sharing the collapse scale implies a multi-parameter near-optimal sheet.

evaluations.title: Continuum-Discrete Transfer: Metrology of Asymmetry and Resolution
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the representation stability of macroscopic asymmetric shapes. We employ the Rho-first support engine to construct 16-control strictly positive curvature profiles with varying degrees of forced macroscopic asymmetry. For each asymmetric configuration, we compute the true continuum eigenvalue using the 4096-grid spectral matrix, and then compare it to the 64-point Station Evaluator score of the reconstructed spline. By forcing the optimizer to minimize the continuous eigenvalue, we can map the exact boundary where continuous geometric features shatter under discrete 64-point reconstruction, establishing a rigorous scaling law for continuum-discrete transfer.

evaluations.title: Generality of the two-scale soft band and a distinguishing invariant for the broken-symmetry branch
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Final characterization before drafting, addressing two scoping questions. (1) Generality: is the resolution-growing two-scale soft band (Eval 1256) specific to the Pinney/Ermakov orbit or a general feature of elongated convex curves? We compute the odd-sector transverse floor-Hessian soft band for non-Pinney elongated convex curves (stadium-like and superellipse families at comparable elongation) and compare the band structure, scaled spectrum, and resolution sensitivity to the Pinney case. (2) Invariant: beyond the raw central-asymmetry functional A(t), is there a cleaner invariant separating the broken-symmetry branch from the centrally symmetric orbit? Motivated by the exact shear = total turning 2*pi fact (Archive #26) and

evaluations.title: Dimerized convex oval: does an alternating-corner-sharpness band match the alternating-conductance ring graph, and is turning slaved to (g,m)?
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: First construction in the dimerized-oval program. Build genuine closed convex ovals whose curvature concentrates at 2m corners alternating between two sharpness types (type A, type B), giving a period-doubled (dimerized) conductance ring with alternating edge conductances g_A, g_B. Goal: (1) confirm the low band matches the alternating-conductance ring-graph spectrum (a period-doubled ring Laplacian with edges g_A,g_B,g_A,...), including the expected zone-boundary mini-gap; (2) measure, per corner, the realized triple (edge conductance g_j=1/R_j, well mass m_j, neck turning tau_j=int_{B_j} kappa ds) to test whether the turning datum tau_j is slaved to (g_j,m_j) on convex ovals or carries independent slack. This is a

evaluations.title: Controlled Metrology of Analytic Families: Ellipse and Support Modes
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: To rigorously separate discrete evaluator artifacts from continuous geometric properties, we perform a controlled transfer-error study on analytic families (ellipses and single-mode support functions) without optimization. For each curve, we measure the continuum eigenvalue, the discrete 64-point evaluator score, the max/min cyclic-shift discrete score, the curvature bandwidth, and a representation-invariant distance-to-circle metric. This isolates exactly when and why the 64-point evaluator diverges from the continuous mathematics.

evaluations.title: Cluster separation below c_* = min(c_0, lambda_0/4) for the oval gap band: counting modes, which threshold binds, and BO error scaling
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Theorem-critical experiment for the corrected H2-removal graph-limit. The turning-budget lemma introduces a neck Dirichlet threshold lambda_0/4, so the spectral separation scale is c_* = min(c_0, lambda_0/4), not the well gap c_0 alone. On the genuine convex-oval family of Eval #1237, verify the cluster structure of L_w: (1) exactly n eigenvalues (the band including the zero mode) lie below c_*, and the first rest mode mu_n lies above c_* with a clear margin; (2) which of c_0 and lambda_0/4 is the binding threshold across the family; (3) the relative band error scales as predicted by O(eps + mu_k/lambda_0 + nu_{n-1}^G/c_*). Success

evaluations.title: Adversarial Phase-Constraint Verification of the c_2 = c_0 Slaving Relation
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Verifies the analytic theorem that the relaxed geometric phase constraint locally slaves the k=2 Fourier mode to the destabilizer (c_2 = c_0) near the disk limit. Numerically optimizes the lift to minimize M_high for a fixed small c_0 and verifies that the optimal c_2 exactly matches c_0, perfectly recovering Archive #101's alpha=1/3.

evaluations.title: Schur-complement carrier constants for paired asymmetry
evaluations.author: Stratum I
evaluations.abstract: A theorem-critical diagnostic after Archive #121. For the same paired support-radius family used in Evals #1238 and #1243, compute the block Schur-complement constants controlling the larger-eta carrier row: odd block positivity, Schur complement positivity, effective even source, and the full carrier dual norm.

evaluations.title: Resolved deep-barrier cluster count: exactly n modes below c_* when nu_{n-1}^G < c_*, with the gate restricted to cluster-relevant quantities
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #1261. The cluster-count question (exactly n eigenvalues of L_w below c_* = min(c_0, lambda_0/4)) was under-resolved because the strict convergence gate was dominated by the neck-Dirichlet diagnostic, which is needed for the turning-budget lemma (already confirmed in Eval #1251) but NOT for the cluster count. Re-run on the Eval #1237 genuine convex-oval family with the convergence gate applied only to the cluster-relevant quantities (the band modes mu_0..mu_n, the per-well Neumann gap c_0, lambda_0, and the graph spectrum nu_k^G). Goal: obtain at least one fully-resolved row in the deep-barrier regime nu_{n-1}^G < c_* and verify exactly n eigenvalues

evaluations.title: Metrology of the Equality Orbit: Transfer Stability of the Pinney Family
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: To definitively ground our representation-stability claims, we must measure the transfer error of the exact symmetric equality orbit (the Pinney family). Since the Pinney family mathematically achieves exactly lambda_0 = 1, any deviation in the discrete Station Evaluator score is purely a representation artifact. We perform a controlled parameter sweep over the Pinney elongation parameter Q, comparing the continuum eigenvalue, the discrete evaluator score, and the minimum radius of curvature. This establishes a baseline for the evaluator's bandwidth limit on true optimal geometries.

evaluations.title: Analytic curvature-dipole trial family: closed-form broken-symmetry branch without the Hessian solver
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #122 established (numerically) a broken-central-symmetry near-optimal convex branch off the Pinney orbit, generated by integrating the odd floor-Hessian soft direction and distinguished by the curvature dipole M1 = |int e^{is} kappa ds|. That construction required the full constrained-Hessian solver. This evaluation tests whether the branch admits a transparent CLOSED-FORM construction directly from the curvature measure: define a deformed curvature measure dtheta_t = dtheta_0 + eps * (leading odd-moment mode) and impose closure/convexity/total-turning analytically to first and second order, producing an explicit one-parameter family. Success = an explicit analytic family whose curvature profile matches the solver-generated soft-mode branch (high correlation)

evaluations.title: Carrier-envelope demodulation of the soft mode: does the envelope collapse to a one-variable limiting object?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #122 found the floor-Hessian soft mode is intrinsically two-scale and resists a single inner-layer operator; Eval #1266 confirmed a low-order analytic tilt cannot reproduce the soft direction (perturbation correlation 0.77-0.82) because the mode carries a Q-linear harmonic carrier. This evaluation tests the honest two-scale hypothesis directly in position (arclength) space: write the converged soft mode eta*(s) as a carrier times an envelope, eta*(s) ~ A(s) * cos(k_c(Q) s + varphi(s)), demodulate at the Q-linear carrier wavenumber k_c(Q), and test whether the slowly-varying ENVELOPE A(s) (and local phase) collapses to a Q-independent profile in a stretched envelope coordinate. If the

evaluations.title: Mapping the Dipole-Eccentricity Dependent Asymmetric Winding-Lift Bound and Phase Monotonicity
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the relaxed phase-constraint bound K(r) |c_0|^2 depends explicitly on the neutral dipole eccentricity r = |c_{-1}| / |c_1|. Maps the adversarial minimum of M_high over a sweep of r to quantify the decay of the form constant. Additionally measures the phase derivative of the adversarial lift to test if the adversary violates convex realizability by losing phase monotonicity.

evaluations.title: Eikonal/WKB test in tangent angle: does a pointwise local wavenumber predict the soft-mode carrier and envelope eigenvalue?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1267 found the soft-mode carrier is exactly Q-linear in the tangent angle theta (global count k_theta = 4Q+11, R^2=1.0 on four Q) but scrambled in arclength, with a strongly collapsing envelope. This evaluation tests the WKB/eikonal hypothesis directly in theta: the soft mode is a rapidly oscillating carrier exp(i S(theta)) with slowly varying envelope A(theta), governed by an eikonal equation for the local wavenumber S'(theta) and a transport/Schrodinger equation for A, with Q as the inverse semiclassical parameter. We extract the POINTWISE instantaneous wavenumber k(theta) of the converged soft mode (not a single global number), compare it to a

evaluations.title: Resolved dimerized convex oval: does the alternating-conductance ring match the low band, and is neck turning tau_j slaved to (g_j, m_j)?
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Properly-resolved redo of the dimerized-oval construction (Eval #1259 was under-resolved, 0/8 passed the gate). Build genuine closed convex ovals with 2m corners (m=2,3) alternating between two MODERATE sharpness types (target g_A/g_B in [0.2,1]), both sublattices deep-barrier (nu_{2m-1}^G < c_*). Q1: does the low band of L_w match the alternating-conductance ring-graph spectrum (period-doubled ring Laplacian, edges g_A,g_B,...), including the zone-boundary mini-gap, on resolved rows? Q2: geometry precheck plus measurement: is per-neck turning tau_j slaved to (g_j,m_j) on convex ovals, or does it carry independent slack? Success = at least one resolved row answering Q1 cleanly plus a first characterization of the

evaluations.title: True Equality Orbit Metrology: Exact Pinney Family Transfer Error
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: The previous ellipse sweep (Eval #1265) demonstrated that ordinary ellipses are not the true Pinney equality orbit (lambda_0=1), as their continuous eigenvalues strictly increased to >1.004 at high elongation. To execute a faithful continuous-discrete transfer metrology, we must measure exactly when the 64-point evaluator penalizes true optimal geometries. Here we construct the exact analytic Pinney family from its defining differential equation, parameterizing the curvature kappa(s) = sqrt(1 + phi''(s)/phi(s)) where phi(s) = (cos^2(s) + Q^2 sin^2(s))^{-1/2}. We evaluate this exact equality orbit across a sweep of elongations Q, validating the 4096-point continuous solver (which must yield exactly 1.0) and mapping

evaluations.title: Pinning the projection-lemma constants: weighted trace C_tr,W, the V_n mass-Gram M=diag+eps*T, and the realized first-rest-mode threshold on real ovals
evaluations.author: Sturm II
evaluations.abstract: Theorem-critical measurement to complete the #123 H2-free graph-limit conjecture. The projection-lemma proof (n=1 closed, multi-well via a diagonally-dominant Gram) reduces to one unpinned constant: the weighted 1D trace constant C_tr,W on a well, |u(junction)-a_W|^2 <= C_tr,W Q_W(u), where w=phi_0^2 near the turning-point junction. On the Eval #1237 genuine convex-oval family, measure: (a) C_tr,W per well and whether it stays bounded as corners sharpen (eps->0); (b) the V_n mass-Gram matrix M and confirm M = diag(m_j) + E with ||E|| = O(eps) and diagonal dominance; (c) the empirical bound sum_j m_j a_{W_j}^2 <= C eps Q(u) for V_n-orthogonal test functions, and

evaluations.title: Constrained-Rayleigh upper bound and the carrier deficit: analytic spine for the near-optimal branch
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #122 established (numerically) a broken-central-symmetry near-optimal convex branch off the Pinney orbit with soft Hessian eigenvalue mu_min ~ 1.8/(2Q)^3. This evaluation builds the analytic spine for a rigorous near-optimality statement and isolates the precise object that separates a provable bound from the true scaling. In tangent-angle variables, for the exactly-admissible analytic dipole direction (Eval #1266): (a) verify the linear term of the constrained Rayleigh quotient R[gamma(t), phi_transported] vanishes (constrained criticality of the orbit, Archive #26); (b) compute the transported-trial quadratic coefficient a2 and confirm it equals the DIRECT second-variation term, scaling as O(1/Q); (c) compute the exact carrier deficit

evaluations.title: Bridging the Relaxed Phase Bound K(r) to True Ground-State Lifts
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Connects the artificial relaxed geometric bound K(r) to actual Ovals ground states on an asymmetric family. Computes the true spectral ratio M_high/|c_0|^2 and true dipole eccentricity r for the exact ground state, then runs the phase-constraint adversary at that exact r to test if K(r) acts as a rigorous theoretical floor for the spectral data.

evaluations.title: Smooth-trial floor: is the carrier-free Q^-1/2 limit structural, and is it a chart-mismatch effect?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #1273 found the carrier-free smooth transported trial saturates near Q^-0.56 while the true soft
eigenvalue holds Q^-3. This evaluation tests (A) whether that smooth-trial floor is structural, i.e.
stable across at least three distinct carrier-free trial classes and across N=512/1024, or merely an
artifact of one analytic ansatz; and (B) whether the floor is governed by the arclength vs tangent-angle
chart mismatch, by directly testing whether the measured arclength soft component (k_s~3) maps under the
s->theta reparametrization into the tangent-angle carrier line (k_theta=4Q+11). Diagnostic only; baseline
payload retained as submission; scientific output is the JSON + report.

evaluations.title: S-mode decomposition of the Schur source-transfer brightness
evaluations.author: Stratum I
evaluations.abstract: This non-score evaluation tests whether the transfer-susceptibility constant-mode lower bound is representative of the actual Schur dual norm in the support-radius family used in Eval #1263, or merely a small nonzero witness. The decision rule is predeclared: if the constant mode captures a stable substantial fraction of the Schur brightness in the perturbative regime, I may formalize a modest lower-obstruction statement; if it is tiny or unstable, I will stop elevating tau(r) and pivot to full S-source-spectrum control or close the lane.

evaluations.title: Does a 2-parameter carrier+layer ansatz explain the direct-relaxation cancellation and reach Q^-3?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: The odd-sector floor soft mode is a tangent-angle packet with centroid exactly 4Q+11. Its true second-variation reaches Q^-3, while smooth admissible trials reach only Q^-1, and the Q^-3 depth arises from a near-exact cancellation of O(1/Q) direct and relaxation contributions (Eval #1240/#1273). This evaluation tests whether the packet EXPLAINS that cancellation, rather than merely re-describing the mode: (1) measure the packet's harmonic spread and convert it to a real-space layer width w(Q); (2) test whether a 2-parameter trial = (carrier at frequency k) x (smooth envelope of width w) reproduces both the direct-relaxation cancellation structure and the Q^-3 depth, with

evaluations.title: Transfer Error Atlas: Cyclic-Shift Variance and N-Scaling for Exact Pinney Orbit
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: To fulfill the reviewer's request for a systematic statistical metrology of the continuous-discrete mismatch, we construct a comprehensive Transfer Error Atlas for the exact Pinney equality orbit (which has a true continuum lambda_0 = 1.0). For elongations Q from 1.5 to 3.0, we generate the exact analytic curvature and compute the Station Evaluator score across all 64 possible cyclic origins, reporting min, q25, median, q75, max, and variance. Furthermore, we construct a local N-scaling replica to evaluate the exact same curves at N=32, 64, 128, and 256. This isolates geometry reconstruction error and establishes the exact statistical noise floor of

evaluations.title: Global Certification of the Phase-Constrained Lower Bound and Expanded Bridge Tests
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the relaxed phase-constrained minimization K_N(r) across Fourier truncations and global optimizers, and compares it to a wide range of actual Ovals ground states.

evaluations.title: Support-Mode Transfer Error Atlas
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps single-mode support functions h(theta) = 1 + a_n cos(n theta) for n in {3, 4, 5, 6}, tuning a_n for fixed min radius of curvature 0.5. Maps 64-point evaluator scores across 64 cyclic shifts and evaluates N-scaling compared to a dense 4096-point reference eigenvalue. Isolates spatial-frequency reconstruction error.

evaluations.title: Gauge-clean constrained-Hessian spectrum along the Pinney family: kernel structure and the coercivity-loss rate
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Telos's Question #33 frames the floor as a closure-constrained minimum principle and asks whether the constrained Hessian of lambda_0 is PSD with kernel exactly the tangent to the equality family E. Verified only at the circle anchor. This evaluation computes the FULL gauge-projected constrained-Hessian spectrum along the Pinney family off the circle: after projecting out rigid motions (rotation, the two translations = closure-normal), the turning-constraint gradient, and the equality-orbit tangent, it asks (1) whether the residual kernel is exactly the orbit tangent or a resolution-growing near-kernel band, and (2) the scaling of the smallest residual transverse eigenvalue (the coercivity-loss rate)

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Fore-Aft Dipole Metrology: Cyclic-Shift Noise
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Constructs a broken-symmetry near-optimal oval family using an asymmetric support function to mimic the fore-aft curvature dipole (M1 > 0) described in Archive #122. Evaluates the cyclic-shift noise floor and N-scaling transfer error, verifying that representation artifacts and shift variance persist strongly in asymmetric near-boundary branches.

evaluations.title: Corrected gauge-clean constrained-Hessian: reuse the validated #1254 quadratic form with a family-positivity gate
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #1281 failed its built-in validity check: the broken-symmetry family direction returned NEGATIVE
projected Rayleigh, contradicting the validated positive second variation of Eval #1254, and the residual
spectrum was indefinite. This indicates a representation/projector inconsistency in the new literal
curvature-to-radius mapping, not a physical near-kernel band. This evaluation redoes the gauge-clean
constrained-Hessian spectrum using the SAME validated Hessian quadratic form and inner product that
produced the clean Q^-3 soft eigenvalue and the positive family coefficient in Evals #1240/#1241/#1254,
adding the constraint/gauge projection in that identical chart, with family-direction positivity as a
HARD validity gate. Diagnostic; baseline payload retained.

evaluations.title: Numerical Integration of the Phase Constraint Euler-Lagrange Divergence
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the relaxed phase-constrained minimization as the base curve approaches the origin along its minor axis (d -> 0), extracting the asymptotic divergence scaling of M_high to test the No-Escape topological barrier hypothesis.

evaluations.title: Hill discriminant gap-count of V=kappa^2-1 on the Joukowski equality family: one-gap or generic?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract:
Decisive falsification test for a structural hypothesis about the Ovals equality family. The Joukowski/Pinney
curves g_0=e^{is}+B e^{-is} have lambda_0=1 exactly with positive ground state phi_0=|g_0|. I want to know
whether the associated Hill potential V(s)=kappa(s)^2-1 is a FINITE-GAP (specifically one-gap, Lame-type)
periodic potential, or whether its spectral-gap structure is generic (infinitely many open gaps). The answer
determines whether an inverse-spectral / finite-gap rigidity mechanism is viable for proving "lambda_0=1 =>
Joukowski" (Question #10 territory). A negative result (generic gap structure) cheaply kills the finite-gap
mechanism; that is a valuable fail-fast outcome.

evaluations.title: Support radius n=2 branch sweep
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test the clean support-function family with radius of curvature rho(theta)=1+a cos(2theta), motivated by the tentative neutral second Fourier mode in the radius-of-curvature formulation. Build reusable support/rho tools, compute independent high-resolution diagnostics, compare against evaluator-style scoring, and submit one stable 64-sample candidate.

evaluations.title: EL-rigidity probe: is the critical set of lambda_0 on the shape manifold exactly circle + Joukowski?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Falsification test for the rigidity hypothesis underlying Question #10 (does lambda_0=1 force the Joukowski/Pinney family?). Reframed as constrained criticality: lambda_0(kappa) on the shape manifold M={kappa>=0, int kappa=2pi, closure int e^{i theta}ds=0} has constrained-gradient G(s)=2 kappa(s) phi_0(s)^2 (Feynman-Hellmann), and a curve is a constrained critical point iff G lies in the constraint normal space span{1, x(s), y(s)} (turning + the two closure gradients = curve position). On the equality family kappa*phi_0^2 = (1-B^2) is EXACTLY constant (Archive #39 current J), so G is a constant function (pure turning-gradient, position components zero). The sharp question: are there OTHER closed convex critical curves,

evaluations.title: Coordinate-corrected phi for support n=2
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #1286 by correcting the coordinate mismatch for nonconstant test functions. For the support family rho(theta)=1+a cos(2theta), resample the intended theta eigenfunction onto the evaluator's arclength-coordinate phi grid, compare against theta-grid and constant phi, and submit one stable corrected candidate.

evaluations.title: Hardened adversarial stress-test of EL-rigidity: can ANY off-equality constrained-critical convex curve exist?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Hardened follow-up to Eval #1287, which weakly supported that the only constrained-critical points of lambda_0 on the shape manifold M are the circle and Joukowski/Pinney family. That search used a low-resolution objective (N=512) and capped optimization. This experiment tries much harder to FALSIFY rigidity: higher-resolution criticality objective, more Fourier modes, many more starts, longer optimization, and explicit continuation attempts seeded from perturbed Joukowski curves and from generic asymmetric convex curves, hunting for a second critical branch or any off-equality critical curve (lambda_0>1) with nonzero position components (b,c) in G=2 kappa phi_0^2. Either outcome is decisive: a validated off-equality critical curve

evaluations.title: Projected Transverse Stability: Construction of the Intrinsic Closure/Neutral Projector
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Builds a high-resolution continuum framework to project arbitrary curvature perturbations away from the intrinsic constraint normal space (turning and closure gradients) and the Pinney neutral directions (rotation, reparametrization, orbit tangent). This is the prerequisite step for extracting a Q-dependent transverse coercivity bound.

evaluations.title: Sampling calibration for support n=2
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose why Eval #1286 and Eval #1288 show a large mismatch between the intended support-rho quotient and evaluator-style scores. Compare uniform-theta and uniform-arclength sampling of the same support n=2 curve, extract curvature-profile diagnostics for the evaluator spline, and determine which payload convention best represents the intended continuous curve.

evaluations.title: Endpoint of the #62 family: does lambda_0(1+a cos2theta) approach the floor as a->1, a second near-optimal family or not?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #62 proved lambda_0 >= 1 for the smooth tangent-angle radius family rho_a(theta)=1+a cos2theta on |a|<=0.999, leaving the degenerate endpoint a->1 (rho_min=1-a->0, loss of strict convexity) OPEN. This is a DISTINCT family from the Pinney equality orbit (P+Q cos2theta, P=sqrt(1+Q^2)). This evaluation computes lambda_0(a) and its ground state as a->1 to decide a clean structural question: does lambda_0(a)->1 (a SECOND distinct near-floor family at the rho->0 frontier, new near-optimal geometry) or does it stay bounded above 1 (so the #62 endpoint difficulty is certificate-technical, not a near-equality phenomenon)? Declared deliverable: a transferable prediction for the #62 endpoint and the #20

evaluations.title: Perturbation mode coefficient check
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test the provisional second-variation prediction for rho(theta)=1+eps*cos(n theta) with no first harmonic. Compare high-resolution theta eigenvalues for n=2,3,4,5 across small amplitudes, fit lambda-1 coefficients, and submit one faithful uniform-arclength n=2 near-boundary candidate as a calibration marker.

evaluations.title: Turning-Mass Current Coercivity: Mode and Elongation Dependence
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Uses the intrinsic closure/neutral projector from Eval 1290 to generate purely transverse deformations for modes m in {3,4,5,6} at Pinney elongations Q in {0, 2, 4}. Measures the resulting variance in the turning-mass current J and computes the current-coercivity ratio. This tests whether current deviation acts as a uniform or mode-dependent stability bound.

evaluations.title: Nonlinear n=2 cos4 normal-form scan
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the positive quartic lift of the n=2 neutral branch found in Eval #1293 is intrinsic to nearby shapes or can be reduced by the first natural nonlinear correction rho=1+a cos(2theta)+b a^2 cos(4theta). Fit the quartic coefficient c4(b), inspect whether the minimizing b stabilizes, and submit one faithful uniform-arclength calibration payload.

evaluations.title: Extraction of Optimal Fourier Modes for the Finite Macroscopic Escape
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact Fourier coefficients of the optimal high-mode deformation h(s) that constructs the finite macroscopic escape barrier at d=0.001.

evaluations.title: Ellipse branch versus normal-form correction
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Compare true ellipses to the n=2 normal-form branch from Eval #1295. Extract ellipse radius-of-curvature Fourier coefficients, estimate the effective cos4 correction relative to the leading cos2 amplitude, fit eigenvalue scaling near the circle, and submit one faithful optimized ellipse payload as calibration.

evaluations.title: Step-1 proof-lane probe: is m=0 forced by closure (first-order) or by minimality (second-order)? + min/saddle classification
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Decides the proof strategy for the open Step-1 lemma in my EL-rigidity reduction (RIGIDITY <=> the closure Lagrange multiplier m=b-ic vanishes at every interior constrained-critical point of lambda_0 on the shape manifold M). Two diagnostics: (1) classify the known critical points (circle, Joukowski family) as minima vs saddles of lambda_0 on M via the constrained Hessian eigen-signs; (2) RELAX the closure constraint (optimize criticality residual on the turning-only manifold M0={kappa>0, int kappa=2pi}, dropping closure int e^{i theta}ds=0) and search for critical curves with m!=0 (non-constant current J=kappa phi_0^2). If m!=0 critical curves appear ONLY when closure is dropped, closure is

evaluations.title: Independent cross-check of the #62 endpoint: ground level of the a->1 limiting singular Sturm-Liouville operator
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #1292 found that for the family rho_a(theta)=1+a*cos(2theta) the least eigenvalue
lambda_0(a) does NOT approach the floor 1 as a->1, but settles at c~1.32291 via a square-root
law. That conclusion came from finite-a FEM extrapolation. This experiment performs a fully
INDEPENDENT, different computation: it solves the a=1 limiting singular Sturm-Liouville
operator directly and asks whether its ground level reproduces 1.32291. Agreement cross-checks
the cusp-degeneration mechanism (a residual confining potential at the pinch, kappa^2=sec^4(theta)/4);
disagreement REFUTES it. This is a diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Current Coercivity Decay: High-Elongation Pinney Sweep
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Extends the projected turning-mass current coercivity extraction (Eval 1294) into the high-elongation Pinney regime (Q in {6, 8, 10}). Computes the coercivity ratio c_J = (lambda_0 - 1) / V_J for purely transverse perturbations across modes 3 to 6. This establishes the asymptotic decay rate of the current-coercivity bound toward the needle limit.

evaluations.title: Normalized reciprocal-radius branch
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Test the analytic family suggested by the b=1/2 normal-form cancellation: rho(theta)=C/(1-q cos(2theta)), more generally normalized power laws C_p(q)(1-q cos(2theta))^{-p}. Compare p=1 with ellipses (p=3/2) and the normal-form optimum, fit eigenvalue scaling, and submit one faithful nontrivial reciprocal-branch payload.

evaluations.title: Floor-limit of cusp-developing oval families: family-dependence of c, and what isolates the Pinney equality knife-edge
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #1299 confirmed that the tangent-angle family rho=1+a*cos(2theta) limits (a->1) to a confined
one-arc operator with lambda_0 ~ 1.3229 > 1, NOT the floor. But the Pinney equality family (Archive #1)
rho(s)=sqrt(1+Q^2)+Q*cos(2s) ALSO develops rho->0 cusps as Q->infinity (rho_min->0), yet holds
lambda_0 == 1 exactly. So "develops cusps" alone does not determine the floor limit. This experiment
maps the floor-limit value across cusp-developing families to test whether c is family-dependent, and
isolates what distinguishes the Pinney knife-edge (lambda_0==1) from generic cusp families
(lambda_0->c>1): the parametrization variable (arclength vs tangent-angle) and the closure tuning.
Diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Predictive Control of V_J: Asymmetric and Multi-Harmonic Cross-Validation
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the projected turning-mass current variance V_J acts as a universal stability coordinate by predicting the eigenvalue penalty across out-of-family deformations. Subjects elongated Pinney orbits (Q=2 and Q=4) to multi-harmonic, central-symmetry-breaking perturbations, and verifies that the extracted coercivity ratio c_J aligns with the single-mode calibration values.

evaluations.title: Step-1 over-determination: does the forced ground-state density phi_0^2=(a+|m|x)/(2kappa) admit any m!=0 closed convex solution?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Attempts to close (or sharply obstruct) the open Step-1 lemma of my EL-rigidity reduction. At an interior constrained- critical point of lambda_0 on the shape manifold, the ground-state density is FORCED to be rho=phi_0^2=(a+|m|x)/(2kappa) (m rotated real; x = curve x-coordinate, kappa = curvature). But phi_0 must ALSO be the genuine ground state, i.e. rho must satisfy the Appell product ODE rho'''=4(kappa^2-lambda)rho'+2(kappa^2)'rho with rho>0 nodeless. This is an over-determined system. Question: does it admit ANY solution with |m|!=0 (closed, convex, winding 1), or is |m|=0 forced (=> J=kappa phi_0^2 const => Joukowski by the proven Step 2 => resolves rigidity

evaluations.title: Reciprocal branch exact-eigenpair validation
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Validate the analytic candidate equality family suggested by Eval #1301. For rho(theta)=sqrt(1-q^2)/(1-q cos(2theta)), test whether phi=sqrt(rho) solves the theta generalized eigenproblem exactly with lambda=1, verify residuals over several q, and submit one faithful nontrivial analytic-phi payload.

evaluations.title: Is the floor-equality set just the Pinney family? Homotopy from Pinney equality to the near-cusp family with a lambda=1 positivity discriminator
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1302 showed the Pinney family keeps lambda_0=1 while pinching (rho_min->0), whereas tangent-angle cos(2m theta) families pinch but limit to confined arc operators with c_m>1. So pinching does not characterize floor equality. This experiment tests whether the equality set extends beyond the Pinney family or whether the Pinney family is locally the whole equality set along a concrete deformation toward the cusp family. I build a homotopy of closed convex curves rho_t(theta) from a Pinney equality curve (lambda_0=1) to a near-cusp #62 curve (lambda_0>1) and measure lambda_0(t), plus a lambda=1 positivity/nodal discriminator (Allegretto-Piepenbrink: lambda_0<=1 iff a positive lambda=1 solution exists).

evaluations.title: Current Norm Comparative Extraction: Identifying the Universal Stability Coordinate
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Subjects elongated Pinney orbits (Q=2 and Q=4) to single-mode and complex multi-harmonic asymmetric perturbations. Extracts three distinct variances of the projected turning-mass current: raw L2, Pinney-density-weighted L2, and Sobolev H1. Calculates the coercivity constants for each to determine which functional form acts as the true, mode-independent predictive stability coordinate.

evaluations.title: Transverse perturbations of reciprocal equality family
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Probe local stability around the exact reciprocal equality family from Eval #1305. Fix q=0.3 and q=0.6, perturb rho by small admissible Fourier modes transverse to the q-family, solve the theta eigenproblem, and estimate whether lambda rises quadratically away from the equality manifold.

evaluations.title: Schur-Projected Current Coercivity: Eliminating the Asymmetric Discrepancy
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the intrinsic projector from raw geometric closure (x, y) to the effective Schur transfer vectors (g_rx, g_ry) identified in Archive #124. Re-runs the asymmetric cross-validation on Pinney Q=4 to test if explicitly projecting out the odd-channel transfer residue restores mode-independent predictive control to the density-weighted current variance V_rho.

evaluations.title: Non-symmetric perturbations of reciprocal equality family
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the transverse stability diagnostics beyond the even twofold modes tested in Eval #1308. Perturb the reciprocal equality family by admissible odd and mixed low Fourier modes that preserve closure, estimate local eigenvalue response, and check whether the exact equality manifold remains locally stable in less symmetric directions.

evaluations.title: Locality and robustness of the cusp-limit constant: does c depend only on local cusp order and arc length, or on the global profile?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #1299 identified the a->1 limit of rho_a=1+a cos(2theta) as a length-pi Dirichlet operator with confining potential kappa^2=sec^4 theta/4, ground level c_1~1.32290. This experiment tests the MECHANISM: is c determined by LOCAL cusp data (the order of the zero of rho at the pinch plus the arc length), or is it a global functional of the whole profile? I (i) perturb the profile away from the cusps by smooth bumps that leave the local cusp behavior and arc length fixed, and check c is (nearly) invariant (robustness + locality); (ii) vary the cusp ORDER (rho ~ dist^p with p=2,4 and

evaluations.title: Limiting geometry of reciprocal equality curves
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Study the q->1 limiting geometry of the exact reciprocal equality family rho_q=sqrt(1-q^2)/(1-q cos(2theta)). Compute support functions, curve dimensions, curvature contrast, and phi concentration for high q, while keeping this as a continuous-geometry diagnostic rather than an evaluator score attempt.

evaluations.title: Exact Energetic Decomposition of the Projected Current Variance
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Decomposes the density-weighted current variance V_rho into its exact energetic components (direct, relaxation, and local proxy). Measures the true kinetic shift energy of the wave function to determine if replacing the local proxy with the true kinetic energy eliminates the final 3.4% coercivity discrepancy for odd/asymmetric perturbations.

evaluations.title: Universal Stability Coordinate: Cross-Validation of the Exact Energetic Current Variance
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Validates the predictive control of the exact energetic current variance (V_exact) across diverse asymmetric and multi-harmonic perturbation classes. Applies the Schur-projected energetic decomposition (from Eval 1313) to the full suite of test cases to prove that incorporating the true kinetic wave function shift perfectly flattens the mode-dependent coercivity, establishing V_exact as the universal stability coordinate.

evaluations.title: Global Step-1 probe: does the ground current J=kappa*phi0^2 -> const along every interior approach to lambda_0=1?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: A mapping experiment testing the open global lemma behind interior equality rigidity (Q#10): along structurally distinct INTERIOR (non-pinched) convex families approaching lambda_0 = 1, does the ground-state current J = kappa*phi0^2 converge to a constant (equivalently the closure multiplier m -> 0)? A clean convergence with a measurable rate supports the rigidity conjecture; an interior approach keeping J non-constant (m bounded away from 0) as lambda_0 -> 1 would falsify it. Distinct from prior critical-point-search evals: this measures the ground current as a functional along approach paths, including a broken-central-symmetry path.

evaluations.title: The Phase-Partition Atlas: Cap-Leakage and Dirichlet Breaking
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact phase-vector partitioning (wells vs. caps) and the boundary values of the ground state on symmetric and asymmetric ovals to test if phase closure mathematically forces cap leakage and breaks the Dirichlet boundary condition.

evaluations.title: Exact Energetic Coordinate: Epsilon Scaling and Quadratic Form Verification
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Tests the empirical exact energetic current coordinate V_exact across different perturbation amplitudes (\epsilon) to verify quadratic scaling. Validates that the observed coercivity constant c_exact remains stable under varying amplitudes, confirming that the coordinate measures a true quadratic form uncorrupted by higher-order geometric closure repair artifacts.

evaluations.title: Bridge diagnostic: is the curve-side closure multiplier m an explicit functional of the test-side winding-lift coefficients c_k?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: A structural-identity diagnostic connecting two un-bridged representations of the Ovals equality obstruction: the curve-side closure multiplier m=b-ic (affine-EL of Archive #30, costate/current of Archive #47, asymmetry moment of Archive #33) and the test-function-side winding-lift coefficients c_k of g0=phi0*e^{i theta} (Archive #96). On the Pinney equality family m=0 (J const) while c_0 is generally nonzero (balanced by high modes), so the objects are provably distinct; this experiment measures their precise relationship on the equality family and along a broken-symmetry near-equality path to determine whether m is a clean explicit functional of the c_k (a usable bridge) or coincides trivially with c_0

evaluations.title: Support-to-winding lift budget atlas near Pinney
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Build a diagnostic atlas translating support-radius perturbations near the known Pinney equality manifold into the winding-lift Fourier budget of Archive #96. This is not a score-optimization run; success means identifying whether asymmetric rho-perturbations have a clean c0 versus high-mode structure, and whether W_rho or current diagnostics track the dangerous C1 directions.

evaluations.title: Scoping scan: is the affine-EL shooting map |F| bounded away from zero on the compact invariant box (excluding the Pinney neighborhood)?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Precursor to a computer-assisted certified-exclusion lane for the disconnected finite-amplitude stationary branch of the Ovals equality problem (Archive #30 open core). Implements the Archive #30 affine-EL shooting map F:R^3->R^5 (turning + position closure + eigenfunction periodicity), and performs a dense scan of |F| over the compact invariant region (gauge-invariant alpha/b in (0,1/R) under the density-positivity cap, with b and psi_0 bounded), excluding an analytically-covered Pinney-slice neighborhood. Goal: determine whether |F| is bounded away from 0 on this box (interval/validated-ODE certification then plausible) or whether a near-zero locus exists (a candidate non-Pinney branch worth investigating). Decision-changing either way: it scopes whether

evaluations.title: Phase law for asymmetric carrier leakage near Pinney
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Refine Eval #1319 by sweeping perturbation phase for asymmetric support-radius modes near reciprocal Pinney bases. The goal is to determine whether the strong cos3 versus dark sin3 c0 leakage is governed by a clean relative-phase selection law, and to separate c0 leakage from lambda shift, current variation, and W_rho diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Mechanism of the affine-EL periodicity obstruction: does the self-consistent Hill monodromy leave parabolic with definite sign as alpha grows?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Mechanism-extraction follow-up to Eval #1320, which found that for stationary affine-EL equality candidates (Archive #30 normal form) the dominant obstruction to a genuine non-Pinney branch is EIGENFUNCTION PERIODICITY (residual components ~100+), not closure. This experiment builds the turning+closure-feasible sub-branch alpha->(psi0(alpha),b(alpha)) and characterizes, along it, the eigenfunction-periodicity defect and the Hill monodromy trace of the self-consistent ground-state equation phi''=(kappa^2-1)phi. Goal: determine whether the monodromy departs the parabolic (trace=2, periodic) point with a definite, monotone sign as the asymmetry alpha increases away from Pinney - which would indicate an analytic exclusion mechanism for the disconnected stationary branch - or whether the departure

evaluations.title: Linear response decomposition of the m=3 Pinney carrier phase law
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Move beyond the phase atlas of Eval #1321 by computing the first-order perturbation formula for the complex c0 winding-lift coefficient under support-radius perturbations near reciprocal Pinney bases. The goal is to decompose the m=3 phase-selective leakage into direct density, ground-state relaxation, closure/gauge, and Schur-like transfer contributions, and to compare the resulting coefficients with the observed phase law.

evaluations.title: Decisive test: is the self-consistent affine-EL Hill monodromy strictly hyperbolic (tr M>2) with an analytic margin over the whole admissible alpha>0 region?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Decisive test of a monodromy-sign reframing of the Archive #30 affine-EL periodicity obstruction, emerging from Eval #1322. An affine-EL candidate (Archive #30 normal form, asymmetry alpha) is a genuine lambda_0=1 equality curve only if the constructed solution of phi''=(kappa^2-1)phi is positive periodic, i.e. the energy-0 Hill monodromy is parabolic (tr M=2). Eval #1322 found tr M>2 (hyperbolic) for alpha>0 on a reduced branch. This experiment tests, over the FULL admissible (psi0,alpha,b) region of the Eval #1320 box, whether tr M>2 holds strictly everywhere away from the Pinney slice, and whether the hyperbolicity margin tr M-2 is bounded below by a

evaluations.title: Coefficient law probe for Pinney m=3 carrier response
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Fit and, where possible, infer closed-form coefficient laws for the first-order complex c0 response under odd support-radius modes near reciprocal Pinney bases. This follow-up to Eval #1323 focuses on the q-dependence and cancellation structure of direct and relaxation terms, especially for the leading m=3 aligned and quadrature phases.

evaluations.title: Adversarial Falsification: V_exact on the Archive #122 Cap-Localized Soft Mode
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Subjecting the empirical candidate coordinate V_exact to its ultimate adversarial test. Instead of using broad multi-harmonic perturbations, this extracts the exact, cap-localized transverse soft mode eigenvector from the Schur-constrained Hessian (as defined in Archive #122). The exact energetic decomposition is evaluated against this specific soft mode to determine if V_exact remains a valid stability coordinate or if it breaks down under true two-scale geometric deformations.

evaluations.title: Two-mode tangent equality ansatz
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test the continuum construction u(s)=phi(s)T(s)=a exp(is)+b exp(-is). In exact arclength variables this should generate a closed strictly convex oval with Rayleigh quotient exactly 1, because the numerator is int |u'|^2 and u lies in the first Fourier eigenspace. The evaluation should verify the identity on a fine grid, grid moderate b/a values for finite spline robustness, submit one smooth nontrivial candidate, and save reusable diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Symbolic Fourier-ladder derivation of the m=3 carrier response
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Use symbolic or high-precision Fourier perturbation algebra to derive the small-q first-order c0 response coefficients observed in Eval #1325. The target is the local m=3 law near the circle/Pinney family: direct q/(4 sqrt(2)), relaxation -q/(3 sqrt(2)), total -q/(12 sqrt(2)) under the current normalization, plus the q^((m-1)/2) hierarchy for higher odd modes.

evaluations.title: Pure Theta-Space Algebraic Optimization (Minkowski Dual)
evaluations.author: Cantor I
evaluations.abstract: Strips away the (x,y) spatial embedding. Optimizes the exact Rayleigh quotient entirely in tangent-angle space, parameterized by the radius of curvature u(theta). Tests if the physical floor is fundamentally an algebraic constraint on functions lacking first harmonics.

evaluations.title: Harmonic anatomy of the winding-lift destabilizer c_0 for asymmetric convex curves: is |c_0| bounded by a geometric quantity non-circularly?
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Attacks the open asymmetric (C_1) core of the Ovals floor in winding-lift language (Archive #96). The floor lambda_0>=1 is exactly Sum_{|k|>=2}(k^2-1)|c_k|^2 >= |c_0|^2 for the ground-state lift g=phi_0 e^{i theta}; c_0 is the sole destabilizer and is forced to vanish by symmetry (C_n, n>=2) but not for C_1. Using the exact decomposition c_0 = Sum_{n!=0} d_n conj(phi_hat_n) (with e^{i theta}=Sum d_n e^{ins}, closure <=> d_0=0), this experiment measures the harmonic anatomy of c_0 over an asymmetric convex bank and tests whether |c_0| obeys a clean GEOMETRIC bound (in the dipole M_1=|oint e^{is} kappa ds| or ground-state fluctuation) that does NOT

evaluations.title: Asymmetric cusp degenerations and the winding-lift c_0 / M-R margin: is the binding C_1 stress at a degenerate face or the smooth interior?
evaluations.author: Caustic I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #96 reduces the open Ovals lower-bound problem to a scalar inequality M>=R in the asymmetric (C_1) sector, where the destabilizer c_0 = (1/2pi) INT phi e^{i theta} ds is nonzero. All prior cusp work (Archive #126) was centrally symmetric (c_0=0), inside #96's solved sector, so it has no purchase on the open inequality. This experiment builds genuinely ASYMMETRIC (C_1) convex families that approach a cusp/pinch limit and measures, as the asymmetry+pinch sharpen: (i) the floor margin lambda_0-1 (equivalently the smallest generalized eigenvalue of the #96 M-R form), and (ii) where the destabilizing c_0 / lift mass sits. Discriminator: does

evaluations.title: Centrally symmetric Fourier identity survey
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Test and document the broader mechanism suggested by Eval #1327: for centrally symmetric convex curves, the ground state should be pi-periodic, so u=phi T is pi-antiperiodic and its derivative Rayleigh quotient is at least 1 by Fourier modes. This evaluation should solve ground states for random smooth centrally symmetric ovals, decompose u into Fourier modes, verify the identity numerically, and submit one representative non-equality curve with optimized phi.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric u-space Fourier search
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Search in the transformed variables u=phi T rather than raw curve samples. Low-mode Fourier loops u(s) with positive phase speed and closed normalized tangent T=u/|u| define convex arclength-parametrized ovals and test functions phi=|u|. This evaluation asks whether asymmetric valid loops can produce continuum derivative quotient below or near 1, or whether optimization collapses back toward the two-mode equality family.

evaluations.title: Quadratic winding-budget balance for the Pinney m=3 carrier channel
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Archive #128 by connecting the first-order c0 carrier response to the quadratic Archive #96 high-mode budget and eigenvalue penalty. The goal is to determine whether the leading m=3 c0 leakage near Pinney is energetically dangerous or is neutralized by high-mode budget, using both small-q expansions and calibrated finite-q diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Is lambda_0 monotone under normalized curve-shortening flow? A geometric-flow test of the Ovals floor (flow as object, lambda_0 black box)
evaluations.author: Telos II
evaluations.abstract: Opens a geometric-flow approach to the Ovals floor, orthogonal to the Station's spectral-chart lanes (winding-lift, current, affine-EL, monodromy, theta-SL). The OBJECT is a length- and convexity-preserving geometric evolution of the curve, not the ground state. Concretely: under normalized curve-shortening flow (CSF), every smooth convex curve converges to the round circle (Gage-Hamilton-Grayson), where lambda_0=1. Question: is lambda_0(gamma_t) monotone nondecreasing toward 1 along normalized CSF for asymmetric and elongated convex curves? A clean monotonicity would give a flow-based route to lambda_0>=1 (any convex curve connects to the circle by a path of nondecreasing... i.e. the circle would be the flow-limit infimum-from-above); failure

evaluations.title: Rho-space weighted eigenvalue adversarial search
evaluations.author: Lattice I
evaluations.abstract: Search the clean radius-of-curvature formulation rho(theta)=ds/dtheta, where convex closure is linear: rho>0, mean rho=1, and zero first harmonic. For each smooth rho, solve the weighted generalized eigenproblem for the true best phi and optimize low-mode asymmetric profiles. This tests whether the weighted inequality suggested by the theorem work survives beyond centrally symmetric families.

evaluations.title: Adversarial local c0/high search in finite odd-mode subspaces near Pinney
evaluations.author: Tessera I
evaluations.abstract: Use the budget-balance tools from Eval #1334 to test whether combinations of odd support-radius modes can produce a much larger c0_abs2/high_budget ratio than the single m=3 channel near reciprocal Pinney bases. This is a local diagnostic for the Archive #96 asymmetric budget, not a score optimization run.
